nluFMnpsV7.one_liner: Proves matching minimax regret bounds for heavy-tailed linear bandits and proposes Hybrid FTRL, which picks direct or linear loss estimates.
nluFMnpsV7.problem: For heavy-tailed linear bandits with polynomially many actions, the best known upper and lower regret bounds differ by a factor that grows with the dimension d.
nluFMnpsV7.method: A new lower bound separates information shared across actions from evidence available only at the optimal action, and matches the known upper bound for N=d^a with a>q/2. Hybrid FTRL estimates each action's loss by a direct or a linear estimate, whichever has the smaller moment bound, and attains the rate on every finite action set.
nluFMnpsV7.key_idea: The lower bound uses reward distributions with two informative magnitudes plus coupling of instances, and Hybrid FTRL chooses per action between direct and linear loss estimates by smaller moment bound.
nluFMnpsV7.evidence: Theory only: a minimax lower bound for N=d^a with a>q/2 matching the known upper bound, and an upper bound for Hybrid FTRL on every finite action set.
nluFMnpsV7.claimed_gains: Improves the previous lower bound by a factor of order d^{1/2-1/q}(log d)^{1/q} for N=d^a with a>q/2, matching the known upper bound.
nluFMnpsV7.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the lower-bound construction and proof, which closes the gap to the known upper bound, is the main contribution and a strong theoretical result.
nluFMnpsV7.main_concern: The scope is narrower than the title suggests, since the lower bound covers only finite, polynomially sized worst-case action sets with small pairwise inner products, leaving canonical sets such as the unit ball open.

D22zAVF9SH.one_liner: Adds a response-calibration loss matching predicted stimulated-minus-blank differences to randomized trials, applied to a conditional flow forecaster (PC-Flow).
D22zAVF9SH.problem: Neural population models trained to forecast activity can predict stimulus effects poorly because the effects are small next to ongoing fluctuations.
D22zAVF9SH.method: Response calibration is an extra training loss for any forecaster that matches the model's predicted stimulated-minus-blank difference to the one measured in randomized trials, using an unbiased sampled estimate and no circuit resets; PC-Flow is the conditional flow-matching instance.
D22zAVF9SH.key_idea: Train the forecaster so its predicted stimulated-minus-blank response difference matches randomized-trial measurements, directly supervising the intervention effect.
D22zAVF9SH.evidence: Simulated circuits across four model families, a controlled benchmark, held-out combinations of eight simultaneous pulses, and two mouse photostimulation datasets with flow and Gaussian forecasters.
D22zAVF9SH.claimed_gains: Calibration lowers state-dependent response error by at least 40% in all four families, cuts a flow forecaster's response error by 62% without changing its forecast score, and PC-Flow predicts held-out eight-pulse combinations with 44% less error than the sum of exact single-pulse responses.
D22zAVF9SH.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the question of whether forecast accuracy suffices for intervention prediction well motivated and calibrating experimentally defined response contrasts a simple, general idea, with comprehensive evaluations and ablations.
D22zAVF9SH.main_concern: The text is dense and hard to follow, and positive evidence is mostly synthetic, with limited confirmation on real biological data and an unclear benefit of the flow model over simpler calibrated predictors.

LMZAwc5IU2.one_liner: Two-stage parametric neural ODE freezes an identified matrix-polynomial operator so the equilibrium Jacobian is preserved exactly across parameters.
LMZAwc5IU2.problem: Parametric surrogates must recover equilibrium stability and post-bifurcation oscillations, but weak growth is hard to resolve and joint fitting lets nonlinear training alter the equilibrium spectrum.
LMZAwc5IU2.method: Stage one identifies a shared matrix polynomial in the operating parameter from normalised early-window trajectory error with stability penalties, then freezes it; stage two adds a neural coefficient matrix through an amplitude gate whose residual is third order at the equilibrium.
LMZAwc5IU2.key_idea: Freeze an identified linear operator and add a gated, cubic-onset neural residual so the deployed equilibrium Jacobian equals the identified operator at every parameter value.
LMZAwc5IU2.evidence: A thermoacoustic Rijke tube, a cylinder wake and a flexible aircraft wing, evaluating stability crossings, boundary locations, nonlinear trajectories and limit cycles, with ablations of gating, freezing and staging.
LMZAwc5IU2.claimed_gains: Recovers the correct number of stability crossings on all three systems and locates boundaries within the reference resolution on the wake and wing and within a tenth of the grid spacing on the tube.
LMZAwc5IU2.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the two-stage construction is simple, well motivated and well matched to the Hopf-bifurcation problem, with substantial physical demonstrations and targeted ablations.
LMZAwc5IU2.main_concern: Nonlinear prediction relies on substantial system-specific loss design, and the test bed is narrow (three single-pair Hopf crossings), so generality to new systems is unclear.

QW90f19k0P.one_liner: Constructs log-precision transformers that compute tree decompositions and simulate tree automata, expressing MSO properties of bounded-treewidth graphs.
QW90f19k0P.problem: The expressive power of graph transformers is poorly characterized, since transformer expressivity is usually studied through simulation of formal languages in NLP rather than graph logics.
QW90f19k0P.method: The paper shows transformers with log n precision and average-hard attention produce distinct embeddings for bounded-treewidth graphs that differ in MSO-definable properties, in near-linear FPT time given a tree decomposition and near-cubic FPT time without one. The proof is constructive: transformers compute bounded-width tree decompositions and simulate tree automata on linear-size node-and-edge token encodings.
QW90f19k0P.key_idea: Show by construction that transformers can compute bounded-width tree decompositions and simulate tree automata over node and edge tokens, which yields MSO expressivity.
QW90f19k0P.evidence: Theory only: constructive proofs with upper bounds on transformer size in terms of input size, treewidth, and MSO formula length; no experiments are mentioned in the abstract.
QW90f19k0P.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the general MSO result a clean contribution that unlocks many graph properties through existing MSO literature, with the tree-decomposition framing compelling and the paper candid about limits.
QW90f19k0P.main_concern: Reviewers question the link to practical graph learning (large FPT constants, a strong structural encoding in a non-uniform setting, non-permutation-invariant tokenization) and note that no converse upper bound is established.

sWkCNk676S.one_liner: LGN-ViT builds a Boolean-only vision transformer with XNOR-similarity top-k majority-vote attention and XOR residual connections.
sWkCNk676S.problem: Differentiable logic gate networks have not been extended to Transformers because attention must be computed with Boolean operations and deeply stacked logic gates are hard to optimize.
sWkCNk676S.method: A logic attention mechanism uses XNOR similarity, top-k selection and majority vote, and XOR residual connections ease optimization; combined with learnable logic gate modules these form LGN-ViT, a unified Boolean inference architecture.
sWkCNk676S.key_idea: Replace dot-product attention with XNOR similarity, top-k selection and majority vote over binary values, and replace additive residuals with XOR, so the whole network is logic gates.
sWkCNk676S.evidence: Experiments on CIFAR-10 and MNIST comparing accuracy, parameter count and estimated logic budget with established logic networks, plus ablations of the training components.
sWkCNk676S.claimed_gains: On CIFAR-10, LGN-ViT reaches 96 learnable logic gate layers, 6.4 times that of the convolutional logic gate baseline, and wider models improve accuracy on CIFAR-10 and MNIST.
sWkCNk676S.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the XNOR-based Boolean attention idea coherent and well written, with targeted ablations supporting the training components.
sWkCNk676S.main_concern: Accuracy lags convolutional logic gate baselines (52.56% for LGN-ViT D768 versus 60.38% for ConvLogic S on CIFAR-10) and evaluation is limited to CIFAR-10 and MNIST.

ztEBx1jRPI.one_liner: PhaseSteer learns a shared family of low-rank internal corrections and selects among them using relative dialogue trajectories for multi-turn safety.
ztEBx1jRPI.problem: In multi-turn dialogue the same internal correction can help one answer and hurt another that needs the same behavior, so fixed steering mishandles clarification versus refusal boundaries.
ztEBx1jRPI.method: With the backbone frozen, PhaseSteer learns a shared correction family and its allocation from complete-response outcomes, using a paired objective that rewards appropriate answers on both sides of a response boundary under separate constraints on quality loss and added harm.
ztEBx1jRPI.key_idea: Select among learned corrections using relative trajectory features (differences between hidden representations across turns), trained from outcomes of full responses with a paired two-sided objective.
ztEBx1jRPI.evidence: The authors' paired benchmark across four backbones against trajectory-conditioned continuous controllers and online LoRA-RL on Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, plus interactive tests on two backbones.
ztEBx1jRPI.claimed_gains: Across four backbones, gains average 4.1 percentage points for assistance-to-clarification pairs and 4.5 points for clarification-to-refusal pairs; on Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct the gains over online LoRA-RL are 2.6 and 3.0 points.
ztEBx1jRPI.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the problem of context-dependent safety responses relevant, the multi-backbone evaluation fairly thorough, and the requirement that both answers in a boundary pair pass a sound guard against blanket refusal or compliance.
ztEBx1jRPI.main_concern: Gains over outside baselines may come from larger training-feedback budgets (a Qwen2.5-72B judge, 1,540 GPU hours per selected run) rather than the method, with no same-budget baselines reported.

B6UlUJSvQo.one_liner: Gaussian-mixture model of heterogeneous response propensities with differentiable aggregation and feedback recurrence, trained end-to-end on aggregate counts.
B6UlUJSvQo.problem: Learning collective response dynamics from aggregate counts requires connecting a population's response distribution to both current observations and future behavior, given individual differences, contact opportunities, and accumulated experience.
B6UlUJSvQo.method: Differentiable Gaussian Dynamics (DGD) combines a Gaussian mixture of response propensities, differentiable aggregation of contact intensity and behavioral probabilities through reparameterized integration, and a feedback recurrence that updates subsequent responses, so aggregate prediction errors train all parts jointly.
B6UlUJSvQo.key_idea: Use reparameterized integration over a learned Gaussian mixture and a feedback recurrence so errors on aggregate counts jointly update the population distribution, observation functions, and feedback parameters.
B6UlUJSvQo.evidence: Four windows from KuaiRand-Pure and Online Retail II, compared against a DeepAR adaptation with a joint-behavior head and historical-distribution baselines, with ablations and controlled experiments.
B6UlUJSvQo.claimed_gains: Lower joint behavioral negative log-likelihood than a DeepAR adaptation using at most one-fifth of its parameters, and learning the distribution reduces behavioral negative log-likelihood by 10.18% relative to a fixed Gaussian in KuaiRand's standard-recommendation window.
B6UlUJSvQo.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree DGD is a coherent, interpretable, end-to-end trainable construction for aggregate-count data whose components are supported by ablations.
B6UlUJSvQo.main_concern: The benefit of the Gaussian-mixture architecture over close alternatives is insufficiently attributed (a matched discrete mixture reaches NLL 1.1339 versus 1.1232), and the one-dimensional latent propensity restricts behavior correlations.

47uri4YDNt.one_liner: Multimodal VAE with normalizing-flow posteriors, Gaussian mixture prior, and pairwise optimal transport alignment for incomplete multi-view clustering.
47uri4YDNt.problem: Incomplete multi-view clustering must uncover cluster structure from data with missing views, and generative approaches need expressive posteriors and cross-view alignment to infer unobserved information.
47uri4YDNt.method: FEMVAE integrates normalizing flows into variational autoencoders for flexible posteriors, uses a Gaussian mixture prior to impose cluster-aware latent structure, and aligns view-specific latent distributions with a pairwise optimal transport strategy. Once trained, the model can recover missing modalities.
47uri4YDNt.key_idea: Condition normalizing-flow posteriors on each view, regularize them with a Gaussian mixture prior, and align view-specific latent distributions by pairwise optimal transport without full cross-view correspondences.
47uri4YDNt.evidence: Several benchmark incomplete multi-view datasets (reviews cite five datasets and several missing rates), with ablations of the flow posterior, GMM prior, and alignment module.
47uri4YDNt.claimed_gains: not stated; the abstract claims consistent effectiveness on several benchmark datasets but is cut off before any numbers.
47uri4YDNt.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find flow-based posteriors with a Gaussian mixture prior more expressive than standard Gaussian assumptions, with optimal transport alignment suited to missing views and promising clustering results.
47uri4YDNt.main_concern: The probabilistic factorization and the theoretical bound do not clearly match the adaptive fusion actually used, and ablations do not isolate each regularizer or report standard deviations.

0rpYxbJGn7.one_liner: Masks low-entropy tokens in the longer DPO response so only high-entropy, preference-informative tokens match the shorter response's token count.
0rpYxbJGn7.problem: Equalizing token counts to fix DPO's length sensitivity leaves open which tokens should contribute to preference learning.
0rpYxbJGn7.method: IAPO uses model entropy as a ranking signal and masks low-entropy positions in the longer response to match the retained token count of the shorter response. The analysis shows true conditional entropy upper-bounds token-level preference information and top-K selection minimizes a discarded-entropy surrogate under a fixed token budget.
0rpYxbJGn7.key_idea: Rank tokens by model entropy and keep only the top-K tokens of the longer response, equal to the shorter response's length, when computing the DPO loss.
0rpYxbJGn7.evidence: Experiments across multiple model families and scales (reviews cite 5 models across 3 families, equal-token-budget comparisons with random-K and bottom-K, and three seeds per method), with matched-budget ablations.
0rpYxbJGn7.claimed_gains: not stated; the abstract only says IAPO improves over DPO and performs well on average against recent variants across model families and scales.
0rpYxbJGn7.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the method simple to adopt, with equal-token-budget comparisons that separate token selection from length equalization and consistent gains across several models and tasks.
0rpYxbJGn7.main_concern: The conceptual advance is narrow relative to SamPO and high-entropy token selection in RLVR, the case for entropy over alternative selection signals is weakly justified, and some gains are within noise.

EkeIrT7Hqj.one_liner: Controlled benchmark showing conflicting peer opinions make LLMs abandon evidence-supported answers, the Peer Override Effect.
EkeIrT7Hqj.problem: In multi-agent LLM systems that exchange conclusions, it is unclear whether a model preserves its own evidence-grounded reasoning when a peer opinion conflicts with the evidence available to it.
EkeIrT7Hqj.method: Builds a controlled benchmark that holds rules, query, and model-visible evidence fixed while varying only the presence of a conflicting peer opinion. Per the reviews, cases are programmatically validated proof graphs with three-way logical classification (entailed, contradicted, unknown).
EkeIrT7Hqj.key_idea: Hold rules, query, and visible evidence fixed and toggle only a conflicting peer opinion, so any accuracy drop isolates the peer's influence on evidence-grounded reasoning.
EkeIrT7Hqj.evidence: 500 cases and 14 LLMs, with the effect persisting across surface realizations and after a model has already produced a correct answer, and with explicit evidence re-evaluation only partially mitigating it.
EkeIrT7Hqj.claimed_gains: Conflicting peer opinions reduce accuracy by 30.45 percentage points; 53.51% of cases answered correctly with evidence alone become incorrect, versus only 4.31% shifting from incorrect to correct, and the effect varies by more than 55 percentage points across models.
EkeIrT7Hqj.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the controlled, programmatically verified benchmark isolates peer influence cleanly and that the experiments across models, message formats, and prompting strategies are comprehensive.
EkeIrT7Hqj.main_concern: The benchmark is synthetic logical tasks with constructed peer opinions, so generalization to realistic multi-agent settings is unclear, and no control separates peer attribution from simply presenting a conflicting conclusion.

YwzGGotBWD.one_liner: Reallocates GRPO's positive credit across successful responses by weighted Nash welfare and refunds penalties on failed-response segments.
YwzGGotBWD.problem: A GRPO update can lower the likelihood of an individual successful response, and repeated, similar successes can dominate the positive update through multiplicity alone.
YwzGGotBWD.method: Nash Credit Routing reallocates a fixed positive-credit budget across successful responses and selectively refunds penalties on failed-response segments while staying near GRPO. Bargaining powers come from minimizing directional collision under a multiplicity-calibrated ratio constraint, then weighted Nash welfare is maximized over normalized likelihood gains.
YwzGGotBWD.key_idea: Allocate a fixed positive-credit budget across successes by maximizing weighted Nash welfare over likelihood gains, with weights from minimizing directional gradient collision.
YwzGGotBWD.evidence: Several models and mathematics benchmarks against baselines, with first-order guarantees relative to GRPO (stated for single-group, full-gradient updates per reviews).
YwzGGotBWD.claimed_gains: Higher macro-average pass@1 and pass@128 than the compared baselines across the evaluated models and mathematics benchmarks; no further numbers stated.
YwzGGotBWD.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers see the credit allocation under explicit constraints as principled and note improved pass@128 on the evaluated model-benchmark pairs.
YwzGGotBWD.main_concern: The paper is dense, the guarantees are not validated against the practical selected-token proxy, and the computational overhead of per-sample gradients is not quantified.

LAhq6RsxnR.one_liner: PLUM represents weights as orthonormal basis times coefficients and updates them with Muon-based Grassmann geodesic steps using only matrix multiplications.
LAhq6RsxnR.problem: Factor-wise optimization of low-rank parameterizations is not invariant to the non-unique factorization, so equivalent representations of the same weight induce different updates.
LAhq6RsxnR.method: Each weight is stored as an orthonormal subspace basis plus a coefficient matrix, separating subspace motion from coefficient changes. Muon's unit singular values make the Grassmann geodesic and momentum transport simple, and a fixed Newton-Schulz approximation gives a GEMM-only optimizer with one momentum state per factor.
LAhq6RsxnR.key_idea: Keep one factor on the Stiefel manifold and update it along a Grassmann geodesic using Muon's matrix-sign step, avoiding matrix exponentials and repeated QR or polar retractions.
LAhq6RsxnR.evidence: C4 pretraining and GLUE fine-tuning up to models over 1B parameters, plus convergence theory for finite Newton-Schulz iterations.
LAhq6RsxnR.claimed_gains: Lower pretraining perplexity than prior low-rank methods on C4 and GLUE up to over 1B parameters (abstract text cuts off); proves an O(T^(-1/4)) stationarity rate and O(T^(-1/2)) orthogonality error bound.
LAhq6RsxnR.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the Muon-Grassmann connection is appealing and hardware-efficient, backed by finite-Newton-Schulz convergence analysis and consistent gains over Spectron.
LAhq6RsxnR.main_concern: C4 gains over Spectron are small (0.13-0.24 perplexity) without multi-seed variance, and training budgets are short (at most 13.1B tokens).

7HbYOsscKa.one_liner: Benchmark for social-context vision-and-language navigation and a socially conditioned world model predicting consequences of candidate routes.
7HbYOsscKa.problem: Existing Social-VLN treats pedestrians as obstacles, ignoring attributes and human-robot interactions that shape pedestrian behavior and social compliance.
7HbYOsscKa.method: They formulate Social Context-VLN, build a benchmark with pedestrian age, gender and human-robot interaction annotations (over 35K episodes, 1.4K pedestrians), and propose SocioWM, a socially conditioned world model that predicts the social consequences of candidate routes.
7HbYOsscKa.key_idea: Condition a world model on pedestrian attributes and interaction responses to predict the social consequences of each candidate navigation action.
7HbYOsscKa.evidence: SocialBench-VLN with scene-disjoint splits, seven recent VLN agents as baselines, and ablations of age, gender and interaction annotations per reviews.
7HbYOsscKa.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers see a real gap between VLN with pedestrians and socially aware navigation, and value the benchmark's structured per-step annotations.
7HbYOsscKa.main_concern: Age and gender effects are hand-coded into the simulator, so the model may learn authored rules, and removing these attributes changes SR by only 0.8 to 1.1 points.

GmBZGIhwxN.one_liner: Multi-view clustering with samples representing anchors, Schatten p-norm anchor balancing, and alternating sample/anchor label updates.
GmBZGIhwxN.problem: Anchor-graph multi-view clustering treats anchor graphs only as sample representations, losing fine-grained structure, and ignores consistency between anchor and sample distributions.
GmBZGIhwxN.method: Samples represent anchors instead of the reverse, and an anchor balancing mechanism based on the Schatten p-norm, backed by theoretical analysis, aligns anchor and sample distributions. Sample labels and anchor labels are updated alternately, with a low-rank tensor constraint on sample labels to capture complementary information across views.
GmBZGIhwxN.key_idea: Reverse the anchor representation direction (samples represent anchors) and regularize anchor assignments with a Schatten p-norm balancing term so anchor and sample distributions stay consistent.
GmBZGIhwxN.evidence: Abstract cites extensive clustering experiments (datasets not named) and theoretical analysis of the balancing mechanism; reviews refer to Theorems 1 and 2.
GmBZGIhwxN.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers credit the samples-represent-anchors reversal, the Schatten p-norm balancing with theoretical analysis, and the alternating collaborative label update.
GmBZGIhwxN.main_concern: The theory may not carry over to the actual optimization (the theorems assume a constraint the optimized variable does not enforce), and ablations of the balancing and tensor terms and convergence curves are missing.

wZ36tYVCcv.one_liner: SCOPE calibrates response sharing across personas and policies from queried answers, then selects queries to reconstruct all LLM-simulated responses.
wZ36tYVCcv.problem: Simulating how a population responds to policies with LLMs needs a costly Cartesian product of personas and interventions, so full evaluation is expensive.
wZ36tYVCcv.method: The paper defines zero-history population-response reconstruction: given n personas, m policies and a budget B much smaller than nm teacher queries, reconstruct the response distribution for every pair. SCOPE is a closed-loop framework that calibrates shared response structure from queried answers and uses it to choose the next queries.
wZ36tYVCcv.key_idea: Learn which personas and policies share responses from observed answers, and use that calibrated structure to pick the most informative next queries in a closed loop.
wZ36tYVCcv.evidence: A hierarchical benchmark of 1,024 World Values Survey personas and 600 COFOG-based policies (614,400 pairs per teacher) with four teacher models; diagnostics plus three-seed mean full-pool error across query budgets; code and data are released.
wZ36tYVCcv.claimed_gains: SCOPE achieves the lowest three-seed mean full-pool error at every reconstruction level across four teachers and all evaluated query budgets.
wZ36tYVCcv.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the task clearly defined and the diagnostics well linked to the method design, with a systematic hierarchical benchmark, ablations and reproducible presentation.
wZ36tYVCcv.main_concern: Evaluation measures agreement with an LLM teacher only, with no comparison to human responses, and one reviewer finds the Table 3 numbers come from a single seed rather than the stated three-seed mean.

3QjD8Nv1A6.one_liner: Learned semantic segmenter plus block distillation from a full-attention teacher to make block attention work for KV reuse.
3QjD8Nv1A6.problem: Block attention improves KV-cache reuse in long-context settings such as RAG, but segmenting text into self-contained blocks is hard and block fine-tuning is inefficient and can degrade performance.
3QjD8Nv1A6.method: They build SemanticSeg, a dataset of over 30k instances across 16 categories, train a lightweight segmenter on it, and propose block distillation with a frozen full-attention teacher plus block sink tokens, block dropout and token-level loss weighting.
3QjD8Nv1A6.key_idea: A frozen full-attention teacher guides the block-attention student, with sink tokens at block boundaries, block dropout over all blocks and loss weighting on block-attention-sensitive tokens.
3QjD8Nv1A6.evidence: Per the reviews, experiments on LongBench and LoCoMo across four models up to 14B parameters, with component ablations.
3QjD8Nv1A6.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the problem is practically important and that block distillation recovers near full-attention performance across models and outperforms plain block fine-tuning, supported by ablations.
3QjD8Nv1A6.main_concern: Comparison gaps: block fine-tuning and distillation are evaluated on different model families, CacheBlend-style KV-reuse methods are not compared, and reported table averages are inconsistent.

agAQ2i7viU.one_liner: Adapts a frozen speculative drafter to new or LoRA-tuned targets by learning linear maps on the target's features.
agAQ2i7viU.problem: Feature-conditioned drafters are coupled to the target model's hidden features, so LoRA adaptation or replacing the target (which can change dimensionality) makes them hard to reuse.
agAQ2i7viU.method: RelaySpec learns a linear transformation of the new target's features while keeping the drafter's transformer frozen, and the maps can be merged into the existing fusion projection with no extra operation per decoding step.
agAQ2i7viU.key_idea: Learn per-feature-stream linear maps from the new target's hidden features into the drafter's expected input space, then fold them into the frozen fusion projection.
agAQ2i7viU.evidence: Qwen3-4B and Qwen3-8B drafter transfers across math, code and chat, Spec-Bench, a Llama3.1-8B target, five LoRA-fine-tuned targets, and vLLM multi-target serving.
agAQ2i7viU.claimed_gains: A Qwen3-4B drafter adapted to Qwen3-8B reaches 94-100% of native throughput (reverse 88-97%), a single mixed fit reaches 99.4% on Spec-Bench, Llama3.1-8B is 1.83× faster than autoregressive decoding, LoRA targets speed up 1.40× on average and up to 2.42×, and vLLM serving gives 2.91-3.83× throughput.
agAQ2i7viU.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that adapting only the feature interface, with maps merged into the existing projection, is a practical way to reuse a drafter across targets.
agAQ2i7viU.main_concern: The ablations do not isolate the map parameterization from optimization effects, and drafter LoRA performs close to the proposed maps (HM 1.418 vs. 1.445) in an appendix comparison.

eRmps7dfDh.one_liner: Allocates per-layer precision during quantization-aware training using a second-order, curvature-weighted sensitivity model recomputed periodically.
eRmps7dfDh.problem: Aggressive quantization degrades LLM performance, and common approaches assign layer precision using quantization-error proxies.
eRmps7dfDh.method: Q-PACE models the loss increase as quantization-noise MSE weighted by per-layer curvature coefficients, periodically re-estimates the coefficients with perturbations across layers, and reassigns precision.
eRmps7dfDh.key_idea: Predict loss increase as per-layer quantization noise weighted by curvature coefficients estimated with forward-only perturbations, then re-solve the precision allocation periodically.
eRmps7dfDh.evidence: Pretraining and supervised fine-tuning experiments on LLMs of up to 4B parameters, compared with NVFP4 heuristic and SNIP allocation per the reviews.
eRmps7dfDh.claimed_gains: Consistently improves over existing recipes and reaches comparable loss at substantially lower total memory budgets; no numbers are stated in the abstract.
eRmps7dfDh.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the forward-only sensitivity estimation is a practical, interpretable way to allocate precision dynamically and yields lower pretraining loss than the evaluated baselines.
eRmps7dfDh.main_concern: Incremental novelty and limited practical evidence: the curvature-weighted error model resembles HIGGS and HAWQ, dynamic allocation exists in SNIP, and average bit budget is not tied to measured throughput or training memory.

W0p7VKbcGO.one_liner: Mechanistic study of a one-layer transformer on multilingual modular addition, showing shared Fourier representations and a sharing-promoting training intervention.
W0p7VKbcGO.problem: How transformers represent shared concepts across languages is not mechanistically understood.
W0p7VKbcGO.method: They train a single-layer transformer on modular addition expressed in distinct vocabularies, analyze its Fourier-based arithmetic, and add a label-based training intervention that encourages representation sharing across languages.
W0p7VKbcGO.key_idea: Languages with disjoint vocabularies share Fourier features for modular addition, and a label-based training intervention that pushes representations together improves cross-lingual generalization.
W0p7VKbcGO.evidence: A toy single-layer transformer on multilingual modular addition with Fourier analysis and training-time interventions; no real multilingual LLM experiments.
W0p7VKbcGO.claimed_gains: The intervention substantially improves cross-lingual generalization; no numbers are stated.
W0p7VKbcGO.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the multilingual modular addition testbed is clean and controlled, isolating cross-lingual sharing because the languages share no tokens.
W0p7VKbcGO.main_concern: Rigor and scope: key results lack plots or tables, 'shared representation' is loosely defined, the intervention may help simply by pooling data, and the toy setting may not transfer to real LLMs.

TZ056WRa3K.one_liner: Transformer where every layer reads past-token representations from any depth through learned mixes in shared KV channels.
TZ056WRa3K.problem: Each Transformer layer normally uses only same-depth representations of past tokens, which prevents reuse of computed information, and cross-layer connections then slow training and prefill.
TZ056WRa3K.method: A learned mixer selects useful depths per context and combines their representations into shared KV cache channels that layers read; cyclic iteration updates interleaved token groups in turn while processing tokens within a group in parallel.
TZ056WRa3K.key_idea: Mix past-token states from different depths into a small set of shared KV channels with a learned mixer, and train via cyclic iteration over interleaved token groups.
TZ056WRa3K.evidence: Perplexity comparisons with standard Transformers at two scales up to 1.3B parameters, plus iteration-convergence tests on a reference model trained with exact autoregressive execution.
TZ056WRa3K.claimed_gains: With a full-size cache it matches a standard Transformer with 50% more layers at the same training tokens, it outperforms matched Transformers with half the KV cache at scales up to 1.3B parameters, and cyclic iteration converges 12.5x faster than standard Jacobi iteration.
TZ056WRa3K.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that sharing a multi-source KV pool across layers is an effective design, giving better perplexity at half the cache and faster prefill than deep-to-shallow feedback baselines.
TZ056WRa3K.main_concern: Quality comparisons match training tokens rather than compute (about double the training FLOPs), and novelty over existing feedback-memory architectures is incremental.

uFxOGURUi5.one_liner: Domain-expert audit of the SciCode benchmark finds and repairs defects that suppressed correct solutions, releasing SciCode-Verified.
uFxOGURUi5.problem: Frontier models cluster near 60% subproblem accuracy on SciCode, and benchmark defects partly cause this compression of scores.
uFxOGURUi5.method: Experts audit all 65 test problems, correct every repairable defect, remove one unverifiable problem, release a corrected benchmark with an itemized audit trail and reproducible grading harness, and re-evaluate twelve models under matched pass@1.
uFxOGURUi5.key_idea: Audit each problem for non-reproducible gold values, over-tight tolerances, hidden numerical conventions and prompt-grader contradictions, then fix specifications and tests without lowering scientific difficulty.
uFxOGURUi5.evidence: A problem-by-problem audit of all 65 SciCode test problems, then re-evaluation of twelve frontier models under a matched pass@1 protocol.
uFxOGURUi5.claimed_gains: The audit finds 264 defects (192 reject correct solutions), and re-evaluation raises subproblem accuracy from 45-60% to 84-98% and main-problem accuracy from 9-27% to 69-92%.
uFxOGURUi5.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the audit is concrete and inspectable, with a per-problem ledger and defect taxonomy, and that many fixes are clearly right and valuable for a widely used benchmark.
uFxOGURUi5.main_concern: The audit lacks external validation (authors alone reviewed, no agreement measure) and the claim that corrections preserve difficulty is not measured, since fixes may add guidance to prompts.

TDT8wlJowQ.one_liner: Self-distills an ultrasound world model from untracked clinical videos and MRI-derived synthetic action-video pairs using pixel-wise Acoustic Sampling Maps.
TDT8wlJowQ.problem: Learning action-observation relationships for ultrasound world models needs synchronized video-pose pairs, which are costly to collect and largely unavailable in routine clinical recordings.
TDT8wlJowQ.method: They adapt a video foundation model into an ultrasound generator conditioned on reference images and anatomical masks, sample masks along programmable trajectories through 3D anatomy to synthesize action-video pairs, and self-distill these into a world model that needs no masks or 3D assets at inference. The Acoustic Sampling Map (AsMap) represents probe poses and imaging settings as pixel-wise 3D sampling positions, beam directions and depths.
TDT8wlJowQ.key_idea: Encode probe pose and imaging settings as per-pixel 3D sampling geometry (AsMap) and learn action following from synthetic pairs made by sweeping anatomical masks through 3D anatomy.
TDT8wlJowQ.evidence: Zero-shot evaluation on real tracked ultrasound scans plus end-to-end robotic ultrasound planning; training uses cardiac and breast ultrasound with labeled MRI volumes (per reviews).
TDT8wlJowQ.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract is cut off before the results)
TDT8wlJowQ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree removing the need for tracked ultrasound data is practical and that AsMap is an interesting pose representation, with solid quantitative and qualitative validation.
TDT8wlJowQ.main_concern: Reviewers say validation is limited to cardiac and breast ultrasound with heavy reliance on synthetic action-video pairs, and that real clinical or robotic tracked-data validation and training details are insufficient.

ynq4cCvxiU.one_liner: Shows pairwise identifiability does not give simultaneous source recovery in nonlinear multi-view CCA, and gives three recovery regimes for SUMCOR.
ynq4cCvxiU.problem: Existing pairwise identifiability for nonlinear CCA does not guarantee simultaneous source recovery with a single encoder per view, and SUMCOR can favor higher-order modes over first-order source directions (representation drift).
ynq4cCvxiU.method: Under an isotropic Gaussian prior and full cross-view latent coverage, they prove three recovery regimes at population global optima: recovery up to an affine transformation under global first-order dominance; Top-r and masked SUMCOR with known overlap ranks under pairwise dominance; and exact affine readouts at finite spectrum-dependent representation dimensions under joint spectral compatibility.
ynq4cCvxiU.key_idea: Spectral structure, overlap-rank information and representation capacity determine whether SUMCOR recovers source directions or drifts to higher-order nonlinear modes.
ynq4cCvxiU.evidence: Theorems at population global optima, with synthetic experiments confirming the predicted recovery regimes and representation drift.
ynq4cCvxiU.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the representation-drift failure mechanism is clearly explained and that the three recovery regimes extend prior pairwise identifiability theory with supporting experiments.
ynq4cCvxiU.main_concern: Reviewers say the guarantees depend heavily on first-order dominance and joint spectral compatibility assumptions and a structured loading model, with the role of each assumption and the recovery criterion not clearly explained.

wbSGHaZThx.one_liner: Adapts simulation-pretrained neural operators to real data by combining source and repair predictions with ridge-fitted weights per Fourier cell.
wbSGHaZThx.problem: Neural operators pretrained on numerical simulations are hard to adapt to real-world prediction, and a single refinement depth does not suit all frequency components.
wbSGHaZThx.method: R2NO finetunes the pretrained operator on real data and freezes it as a source prediction, while a shared repair module learns a sequence of refinements. Using orthogonal Fourier projections, a spectral ensemble fits a small ridge regression within each cell (defined by radial range, angular sector and measured channel) and combines the refinements by weights fitted on a held-out split, with the source prediction included as a candidate in every cell.
wbSGHaZThx.key_idea: Choose refinement depth per Fourier cell by ridge-fitting combination weights over frozen-source and repair outputs on held-out real data.
wbSGHaZThx.evidence: All RealPDEBench systems and six backbones, compared with full finetuning and iterative refinement (IRNO).
wbSGHaZThx.claimed_gains: Consistently outperforms full finetuning and iterative refinement on all RealPDEBench systems and six backbones (no numbers in the abstract; a review cites summed gains of 14.5% RMSE and 20.6% fRMSE).
wbSGHaZThx.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the method is model-agnostic, motivated by the observation that different Fourier regions favor different refinement depths, and consistently beats baselines across backbones.
wbSGHaZThx.main_concern: Reviewers say gains are dominated by the Cylinder task and lack error bars, the per-frequency refinement claim is not isolated from per-cell weighting or a best-depth-per-region baseline, and R2NO fits weights on extra held-out real data.

ewLDXGTHGt.one_liner: Controlled study of which KV-cache compressions continued pretraining can repair, showing recovery metrics hide multi-key retrieval loss.
ewLDXGTHGt.problem: It is unclear whether continued pretraining restores retrieval after retrofitting pretrained transformers with smaller KV caches, since loss and commonsense recovery may not predict retrieval.
ewLDXGTHGt.method: They compare head merging, joint low-rank compression of keys and values, and token pooling at matched cache sizes and training budgets on Qwen3 0.6B-8B and Falcon3-1B, extend the merge to five model families, and evaluate each conversion against an unconverted control trained with the same recipe.
ewLDXGTHGt.key_idea: Compare conversions at matched cache size and budget against same-recipe unconverted controls, using multi-key retrieval (distinguishing a target key from many similar ones) as the criterion.
ewLDXGTHGt.evidence: Qwen3 0.6B-8B and Falcon3-1B plus five model families spanning 0.6B-14B, at 4K and 16K token contexts, with an exact-inverse value-head rotation test.
ewLDXGTHGt.claimed_gains: At 4K tokens and half the cache, a low-rank latent retains 97.9% of the control's multi-key retrieval at 4B versus 34.0% for head merging, despite similar commonsense performance.
ewLDXGTHGt.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the controlled comparison shows that language-modeling loss, commonsense and single-needle recovery can stay near the control while multi-key retrieval collapses.
ewLDXGTHGt.main_concern: Reviewers say conclusions reflect a small training budget and a single recipe tuned on Qwen3 rather than the conversions themselves, and the paper's main claims are hard to identify and not all well supported.

ZbCTrpmMjm.one_liner: Target-aware SAM optimizer adds the normalized orthogonal residual of a class-reweighted gradient to the SAM perturbation for federated active learning.
ZbCTrpmMjm.problem: Under global class imbalance in federated active learning, aggregate labeled class proportions differ from the target prior, and existing methods improve sample acquisition but leave this mismatch unaddressed in local training.
ZbCTrpmMjm.method: At each acquisition phase, FalOTS builds class weights from the ratio of the target prior to the current global labeled prior, computes a target-aware gradient on each labeled mini-batch, and adds its normalized orthogonal residual to the SAM perturbation. The descent step still uses the original unweighted loss.
ZbCTrpmMjm.key_idea: Add the normalized component of a prior-reweighted gradient that is orthogonal to the empirical gradient to the SAM perturbation, keeping the unweighted loss for descent.
ZbCTrpmMjm.evidence: Analysis of the correction's geometric properties with sufficient conditions; reviewers cite experiments on multiple datasets, ablations on orthogonality, comparisons with class-aware SAM variants, and efficiency tests.
ZbCTrpmMjm.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the problem (global class imbalance distinct from client heterogeneity) is well motivated and the method is simple and clearly presented, with a thorough evaluation.
ZbCTrpmMjm.main_concern: The theoretical benefit over other SAM variants is unclear, the proposition's condition is not checked empirically, and the orthogonal correction is not shown to beat simpler target-prior weighting or class-balanced training.

C5WK3OsFhC.one_liner: Maximum-entropy RL with one-step implicit policies, estimating policy log-density via a separate energy model self-normalized by a Gaussian anchor.
C5WK3OsFhC.problem: MaxEnt RL needs the policy log-density, which is intractable for expressive implicit generative policies.
C5WK3OsFhC.method: SNARL is an off-policy framework that learns a separate state-conditioned energy model to estimate the policy's negative log-density from samples, using spatial and temporal score matching plus an anchor from the Gaussian limit of variance-preserving corruption. A one-step pushforward actor generates each action in a single network evaluation.
C5WK3OsFhC.key_idea: Train a state-conditioned energy model with score matching and a Gaussian-limit anchor that approximately normalizes it online, decoupling log-density estimation from one-step action generation.
C5WK3OsFhC.evidence: Experiments on high-dimensional continuous-control benchmarks including MuJoCo Playground humanoid locomotion against diffusion and flow baselines and DIME; reviewers also cite normalization tests on a 2D Gaussian mixture and a 29-dimensional tracking test.
C5WK3OsFhC.claimed_gains: Competitive with strong diffusion and flow baselines, excels on MuJoCo Playground humanoid locomotion, and gives approximately 14x faster policy inference than DIME.
C5WK3OsFhC.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the problem is important, Gaussian anchoring is a reasonable way to normalize the energy model online, and results are competitive with low action-inference latency.
C5WK3OsFhC.main_concern: Energy-estimation accuracy is validated mainly on synthetic or controlled settings rather than the evolving real policy, and novelty over Dual Score Matching and the uncited AR-DAE is limited.

vmw6y7uIpk.one_liner: Benchmark testing whether vision-language models report every character edit between two layouts of the same document.
vmw6y7uIpk.problem: It is unclear whether VLMs can exhaustively report textual revisions when a document's layout also changes, which matters for contracts and financial reports.
vmw6y7uIpk.method: ReflowDiff has 4,488 comparison tasks built from 374 dense rich-text pages across six generated domains, real web pages, and financial reports; each page is rendered in two layouts and the same one to five character edits are applied to both. Two no-edit controls (Identical, Reflow only) test false reports, and exact match is the primary metric.
vmw6y7uIpk.key_idea: Render each page in two layouts, apply identical 1-5 character edits to both, and score exact match of the full edit set, with no-edit controls to catch false reports.
vmw6y7uIpk.evidence: Evaluation of 30 configurations of 26 VLMs on the benchmark.
vmw6y7uIpk.claimed_gains: The best configuration reaches 76.4% exact match with edits plus reflow; reflow lowers exact match in all 30 configurations, including a 3.8-percentage-point drop for the strongest.
vmw6y7uIpk.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the benchmark is well controlled, the evaluation across 26 VLMs is comprehensive, and the findings expose failure patterns beyond aggregate accuracy.
vmw6y7uIpk.main_concern: Edits are programmatically generated single-character changes on mostly generated documents, and reflow changes layout, wrapping, and font size together, so generalization to real revisions and the cause of the degradation are not established.

3aZ4M2ALyy.one_liner: Robot manipulation model predicts a virtual camera trajectory and queries a geometry-conditioned world model to imagine views as memory.
3aZ4M2ALyy.problem: Clutter, occlusion, and changing viewpoints obscure the spatial relationships manipulation needs, so strong results in structured environments do not transfer to open-world conditions.
3aZ4M2ALyy.method: AWAM predicts task-related virtual camera motion and uses it as a query into a geometry-conditioned world model, producing a spatial prior that is compressed into a fixed memory. The memory is fused with live observations by cross-attention for diffusion-based action prediction.
3aZ4M2ALyy.key_idea: Predict a virtual camera trajectory, imagine the views along it with a geometry-conditioned world model, and cache the compressed result as memory fused with live observations via cross-attention.
3aZ4M2ALyy.evidence: Evaluated on LIBERO-Occ, LIBERO-Plus, RLBench-OG Occlusion1, and real-robot trials, with ablations including learned trajectories versus uniformly sampled spherical viewpoints.
3aZ4M2ALyy.claimed_gains: 75.9% on LIBERO-Occ, 62.4% on LIBERO-Plus, 76.5% on RLBench-OG Occlusion1, and 94.4% in real-robot trials.
3aZ4M2ALyy.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that virtual active perception with a world-model memory is an interesting, practical way to handle occlusion, evaluated in both simulation and the real world.
3aZ4M2ALyy.main_concern: The trajectory predictor imitates demonstrated wrist-camera paths rather than optimizing visibility or information gain, and ablations lack stronger viewpoint-selection baselines, so the benefit of trajectory-based planning is not justified.

usyqufeeti.one_liner: Action-conditioned latent-state world model for time series, trained on factual trajectories only, rolled forward under candidate actions.
usyqufeeti.problem: Time-series models that condition on known future inputs predict the realized future but are not built to predict how outcomes change under different actions from the same history.
usyqufeeti.method: ActTime updates variable-specific latent states through an action-conditioned transition and corrects them with observations over the history, then rolls the same transition forward under candidate actions. Training uses only factual trajectories, without paired alternative-action outcomes or planning supervision.
usyqufeeti.key_idea: Share one action-conditioned latent transition for both observation-corrected history filtering and forward rollout under candidate actions, per variable with cross-variable interactions.
usyqufeeti.evidence: Simulator-grounded suite across building energy, traffic, greenhouse climate, and inventory management, covering factual prediction, intervention-effect prediction, offline decision making, and closed-loop planning, against ten methods.
usyqufeeti.claimed_gains: Ranks first in 12 of 16 domain-task settings; the mean pairwise model-ranking reversal rate is 18.6% between factual prediction and intervention fidelity and 29.4% between intervention fidelity and decision ranking.
usyqufeeti.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the four-domain evaluation separating factual prediction, intervention fidelity, and decision quality is systematic, and the ranking-reversal analysis is useful.
usyqufeeti.main_concern: Methodological novelty over RSSM, MTS3, and recent related work is unclear, and ablations do not consistently support the components (for example, simple action concatenation beats the full model on SUMO intervention prediction).

39d6pLtaDF.one_liner: Image harmonization as predicting a source-relative log-ratio relighting field with Phong-inspired ambient, diffuse, and specular pathways, then analytical reconstruction.
39d6pLtaDF.problem: Existing harmonization methods learn the target appearance directly, forcing appearance adjustment and content preservation into the same prediction process.
39d6pLtaDF.method: Ratio-RFE represents the source-to-target change as a log-ratio relighting field that cancels the shared foreground reflectance, then reconstructs the harmonized foreground analytically from the source. Three Phong-inspired Ambient-Diffuse-Specular pathways learn global tone, spatially varying shading, and localized highlights, combined by an ADS-guided module (ADS-MK) with learned mixing weights.
39d6pLtaDF.key_idea: Predict the log-ratio between harmonized and source foreground, which cancels shared reflectance, and apply it analytically to the source instead of predicting absolute appearance.
39d6pLtaDF.evidence: Reviewers cite results on iHarmony4 and cross-dataset evaluation on ccHarmony, with ablations of the three branches and the dynamic aggregation.
39d6pLtaDF.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the log-ratio relighting-field formulation is a straightforward new modeling perspective, and the three branches and dynamic aggregation improve results on iHarmony4 with cross-dataset generalization.
39d6pLtaDF.main_concern: There is no evidence that the three Phong-inspired pathways learn the ambient, diffuse, and specular components they are named after.

RiBSIEeIEn.one_liner: Theory showing safety penalties can fail after decentralized extraction in offline MARL, plus Deployed-Cost Projection to correct the target.
RiBSIEeIEn.problem: In offline MARL, fitting independent per-agent policies to a joint target changes which actions co-occur and which states are visited, so a stronger safety penalty can lower training-target cost while raising deployed cost.
RiBSIEeIEn.method: Deployed-Cost Projection (DCP) adjusts the joint target using the gradient of deployed cost, preserves the state-flow constraints, and refits the local policies. The paper derives the gradient and gives cost-reduction conditions when the gradient, projection, and policy fitting are approximate.
RiBSIEeIEn.key_idea: Move the joint target along the gradient of the deployed policy's cost, project back onto state-flow constraints, and refit per-agent policies.
RiBSIEeIEn.evidence: Theorems in a one-state KL-regularized setting with binary actions and costs (reversal examples need at most four joint actions), a classification of costs, and experiments on a structured safety task with up to 64 agents with controlled covariance comparisons.
RiBSIEeIEn.claimed_gains: In a structured safety task with up to 64 agents, DCP reaches budgets that penalty increases cannot reach; no numerical gains are stated in the abstract.
RiBSIEeIEn.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the theoretical characterization of penalty reversal and cost floors is clear and new, and the experimental controls help explain the method.
RiBSIEeIEn.main_concern: Experiments are limited and lack comparison with closely related safe offline MARL methods, and local cost reduction is not shown to reach a feasible budget while reward loss during correction is unbounded.

LFTfgeBVb3.one_liner: INT4 KV-cache quantization with INT8 protection of attention sinks and recent tokens to speed up asynchronous RLVR rollouts.
LFTfgeBVb3.problem: Asynchronous RLVR rollouts at high concurrency make KV cache processing the per-step bottleneck (KV concentration), and plain INT4 KV quantization degrades learning even with importance correction.
LFTfgeBVb3.method: KV4-RL combines calibration-free INT4 KV quantization with selective INT8 protection of attention sinks and recent context. This bounded protection reduces sampler mismatch while keeping execution efficient over the compressed cache.
LFTfgeBVb3.key_idea: Quantize the KV cache to INT4 but keep attention-sink and recent-context tokens in INT8 to bound sampler mismatch during RL rollouts.
LFTfgeBVb3.evidence: Abstract: four base models spanning dense and MoE architectures, matched BF16 workloads, BF16 evaluation, three training runs per configuration; reviewers describe Qwen3-4B and Qwen3-8B experiments on an in-house execution stack.
LFTfgeBVb3.claimed_gains: 1.62-1.88x cumulative rollout acceleration and 1.27-1.42x overall training speedup under matched BF16 workloads, with final-policy mean accuracy within 0.8 percentage points of BF16-rollout training.
LFTfgeBVb3.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the KV-concentration analysis identifies a real systems bottleneck and that the end-to-end speedups, with selective protection recovering the INT4 accuracy loss, are convincing.
LFTfgeBVb3.main_concern: Evaluation is narrow (small Qwen3 models, one in-house stack and hardware platform) and the technique looks like a migration of existing mixed-precision and Hadamard-rotation KV quantization.

rKqrMInL2d.one_liner: Extends Drifting Models to categorical data via a Bregman-divergence (mirror-descent) logit update instead of Euclidean additive updates.
rKqrMInL2d.problem: Drifting Models use a Euclidean locality constraint that gives additive sample-space updates, which suits continuous data but not categorical variables on the simplex.
rKqrMInL2d.method: CatDrift replaces the Euclidean penalty with a Bregman divergence, turning the drifting update into a mirror-descent step. For negative entropy it builds a kernel-weighted positive-minus-negative field from real samples and generator outputs, adds it to logits, applies softmax, and regresses to the frozen target by cross-entropy.
rKqrMInL2d.key_idea: With a negative-entropy Bregman divergence, the drifting update becomes a closed-form logit-space step: add a kernel-weighted positive-minus-negative field to logits, softmax, and fit by cross-entropy.
rKqrMInL2d.evidence: One-step generation on discrete image, molecular, and DNA sequence generation without distilling diffusion models; reviewers cite MNIST and CIFAR-10 for images.
rKqrMInL2d.claimed_gains: Competitive-to-state-of-the-art one-step results on discrete image, molecular, and DNA sequence generation; no numbers are stated in the abstract.
rKqrMInL2d.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree this is a clear, well-motivated extension of drifting models to categorical data with a simple closed-form softmax update, evaluated on image, molecule, and DNA tasks.
rKqrMInL2d.main_concern: The locality kernel depends on a pretrained MAE feature extractor without a sensitivity ablation, and the gains are not isolated from the other changes relative to the original Drifting Models.

Gqo0cDeps8.one_liner: Characterizes the maximal parameter-space symmetry groups of LoRA, prefix tuning, and prompt tuning in multihead attention.
Gqo0cDeps8.problem: Parameter-efficient fine-tuning parameterizations contain redundancies where distinct parameter settings represent exactly the same function, which confounds linear mode connectivity and model merging comparisons.
Gqo0cDeps8.method: The paper derives the symmetry groups of LoRA, prefix tuning, and prompt tuning in multihead attention, including RoPE effects, with maximality results under explicit assumptions. Reviewers describe an alignment method built on these symmetries for linear mode connectivity and LoRA merging.
Gqo0cDeps8.key_idea: Identify the group of function-preserving reparameterizations of each PEFT method (for example GL(r) for LoRA) and align models over it before interpolation or merging.
Gqo0cDeps8.evidence: Group-theoretic derivations with maximality proofs; reviewers report experiments on vision and language tasks where symmetry-aware alignment reduces loss barriers for linear mode connectivity and supports LoRA merging.
Gqo0cDeps8.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the group-theoretic characterization of PEFT symmetries, including RoPE, is rigorous and a meaningful theoretical extension, with alignment reducing interpolation barriers.
Gqo0cDeps8.main_concern: The theory relies on restrictive assumptions (LoRA on Q/V only, rank and invertibility conditions, a single attention module), and the O(r)-restricted alignment and merging evidence are limited, with alignment failing for prompt tuning.

z3D5Lp0T0g.one_liner: Mixture-of-Agents with a ranked cross-layer reasoning memory and routing that shows each agent different successful and failed traces.
z3D5Lp0T0g.problem: Existing MoA variants fail to sustain gains as depth increases, showing degradation, early plateauing, or saturation on most benchmarks.
z3D5Lp0T0g.method: ReM-MoA stores and ranks reasoning traces from all layers in a Ranked Reasoning Memory using a comparative Reviewer Agent, and a Curated Diversified Memory Routing scheme exposes different agents to distinct combinations of successful and failed traces. An optional multi-domain Reviewer distillation pipeline uses frontier-model supervision to improve ranking.
z3D5Lp0T0g.key_idea: Persist all layers' reasoning traces in a memory ranked by a comparative Reviewer Agent, and route different top and bottom trace combinations to different agents to keep diversity.
z3D5Lp0T0g.evidence: Five reasoning benchmarks spanning math, formal logic, code, knowledge, and commonsense, under both depth and width scaling against prior MoA variants.
z3D5Lp0T0g.claimed_gains: Consistently outperforms prior MoA variants and, as depth grows, gains nearly three times as much accuracy per additional token as any baseline.
z3D5Lp0T0g.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the reasoning-memory idea is intuitive and clearly written, with consistent gains over MoA baselines on five benchmarks that are not attributed solely to extra compute.
z3D5Lp0T0g.main_concern: Novelty over VeriMoA is limited, the mixed top/bottom routing is not ablated against top-n-only routing, and the cross-layer comparability of Reviewer scores is not verified.

epVuCJPQLq.one_liner: Proves a dimension-free Gamma(1/2) concentration bound for KL instability of softmax decisions under correlated Gaussian score noise.
epVuCJPQLq.problem: The stability of Gibbs (softmax) distributions under correlated Gaussian estimation errors in their scores lacks a sharp, dimension-independent concentration bound.
epVuCJPQLq.method: The forward KL between population and noisy Gibbs distributions is written as a nonlinear log-partition remainder after removing the first-order response to the score error, and its centered positive moment-generating function, normalized by the largest pairwise score-difference variance, is bounded by that of a Gamma(1/2) variable. The proof combines decreasing covariance envelopes under Gaussian smoothing with a bound on the nonzero average gradient caused by asymmetric priors.
epVuCJPQLq.key_idea: Bound the centered positive MGF of the KL log-partition remainder by a Gamma(1/2) MGF using decreasing covariance envelopes under Gaussian smoothing.
epVuCJPQLq.evidence: Proofs for arbitrary finite action sets, reference probabilities, temperatures, correlations, and noise magnitudes, with a balanced two-action problem approaching equality in the small-noise limit, plus numerical experiments on tightness.
epVuCJPQLq.claimed_gains: Yields high-probability KL certificates and O(1/epsilon) sample-complexity bounds, with extensions to unknown covariance, structured action spaces, and entropy-regularized planning; no empirical gains are stated.
epVuCJPQLq.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the main theorem is a relevant, sharp, dimension-independent result for softmax policies built from estimated scores.
epVuCJPQLq.main_concern: One reviewer found the paper extremely hard to read, and others note the certificates may be loose because the scale is set by the worst action pair and experiments use only synthetic noise.

6E6432FEEO.one_liner: Paired empirical comparison of Codex against purpose-built LLM agents on 20 non-coding benchmarks using the same backbone and grader.
6E6432FEEO.problem: It is unclear whether general-purpose coding agents are now strong enough to make purpose-built agent engineering obsolete, since published scores differ in backbone model and evaluation protocol.
6E6432FEEO.method: For each of 20 non-coding benchmarks (finance, clinical reasoning, data analysis, information retrieval, scientific research), an AI-assisted procedure finds a comparable purpose-built agent with released code, verifies its reported score, and re-runs it with the same language model as Codex. Both agents are scored on the same instances by the same grader.
6E6432FEEO.key_idea: Re-run released purpose-built agents with the same backbone model, instances, and grader as Codex to isolate agent design from backbone and evaluation protocol.
6E6432FEEO.evidence: Paired comparisons across 20 non-coding benchmarks with shared instances and graders; reviewers cite paired tests, confidence intervals, leakage checks, and trace analysis.
6E6432FEEO.claimed_gains: Codex significantly outperforms on 5 benchmarks, shows no significant difference on 13, and underperforms on 2.
6E6432FEEO.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that re-running specialized agents with a shared backbone, instances, and graders across 20 benchmarks is a meaningful and more interpretable evaluation than comparing published scores.
6E6432FEEO.main_concern: Conclusions about coding agents in general exceed the evidence from one Codex version, one backbone, and one reasoning setting, and auxiliary models, tools, and judges still differ between the compared agents.

dI6BJscviP.one_liner: On-policy distillation using only the teacher's ranked top-k token IDs, with a fixed distribution over ranks and no logits.
dI6BJscviP.problem: Conventional on-policy distillation reads numerical teacher probabilities at each token, which are unavailable when only partial teacher information can be accessed.
dI6BJscviP.method: LadderOPD keeps the student's probability mass within the teacher's ranked top-k candidate set and favors higher-ranked candidates at uncertain positions through a fixed distribution over ranks. A GroundKL analysis motivates this by showing the OPD signal is concentrated where the student is uncertain and teacher ranks track it.
dI6BJscviP.key_idea: Supervise the student with a fixed rank-based target over the teacher's top-k token IDs at student-uncertain positions, replacing teacher probabilities.
dI6BJscviP.evidence: Five teacher-student settings on GSM8K, three-seed 600-update runs on GSM8K and MATH500, controlled comparison with top-1 targets, gradient-agreement measurements against full-probability OPD, and code generation, single-turn function calling, and a 14B student.
dI6BJscviP.claimed_gains: Statistically equivalent to probability-based OPD within three percentage points on GSM8K across five settings, and reaches 75.18% on GSM8K and 53.87% on MATH500 in three-seed 600-update runs.
dI6BJscviP.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that asking how little teacher information on-policy distillation needs is practical and interesting, and LadderOPD matches full-logit OPD across several teacher-student settings.
dI6BJscviP.main_concern: The rank-only teacher-access scenario is not shown to be practically common, and the paper does not explain why partial information sometimes beats full logits.

HxpxWHG5Xe.one_liner: Learns tool-versus-reason routing for software agents by comparing paired counterfactual branches from the same restored state.
HxpxWHG5Xe.problem: Terminal task rewards give limited credit to individual tool calls: successful trajectories may contain redundant calls and failed ones may contain essential calls.
HxpxWHG5Xe.method: At selected decision states, CNO restores the same agent and repository state into two isolated branches, runs a proposed tool call in one and a reasoning step in the other, and completes both under a shared frozen policy. Their return difference, accounting for task completion, protocol compliance, and optional-call cost, is a soft necessity target learned by a necessity head that guides routing at deployment without counterfactual rollouts, with an obligation mask enforcing required interactions.
HxpxWHG5Xe.key_idea: Train a necessity head on the return difference between a tool-call branch and a reasoning branch rolled out from an identical restored state under a frozen policy.
HxpxWHG5Xe.evidence: SWE-bench Verified and SWE-Bench Pro against outcome-only RL and other baselines, with ablations (exact state restoration, matched suffix sampling, full completion, unpaired value head, mask-only), plus a theorem on unbiased paired estimation and routing regret of at most H times epsilon.
HxpxWHG5Xe.claimed_gains: On SWE-bench Verified, resolution improves from 38.8% to 45.8% over outcome-only reinforcement learning while reducing optional calls per resolved issue; the size of the call reduction is not stated.
HxpxWHG5Xe.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that comparing tool and reasoning branches from the same state addresses a real credit-assignment problem and improves resolution and tool use on SWE-bench Verified and Pro.
HxpxWHG5Xe.main_concern: Each target requires two full suffix rollouts, and the comparison matches only training instances rather than total rollouts, tokens, or compute, so the fairness of the gains is unclear.

9Yl8dL4yC9.one_liner: Models a virtual face identity as a learned distribution over photographic occasions via a shared conditional normalizing flow.
9Yl8dL4yC9.problem: Face generators treat each identity as a fixed point and add variation by prescribed rules, so the form of an identity's variation is fixed by the method rather than learned from data.
9Yl8dL4yC9.method: FAMILIAR first learns an occasion space through identity-conditioned image synthesis without an attribute inventory, then a conditional normalizing flow shared across identities predicts a full occasion distribution from a recognition embedding alone. A newly sampled identity thus arrives with its own repertoire without reference photographs.
9Yl8dL4yC9.key_idea: Learn person-specific appearance variation as a recognition-embedding-conditioned normalizing-flow density over a learned occasion space, instead of prescribing perturbation rules.
9Yl8dL4yC9.evidence: Reviewers cite a controlled comparison of occasion priors (empirical, unconditional, Gaussian, mixture, conditional flow) with generator, identities, and image count fixed, plus cross-photograph and covariance controls and recognition accuracy on synthetic data.
9Yl8dL4yC9.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the cognitively motivated idea of learning identity-specific variation is compelling and the occasion-prior comparison in Table 2 is well controlled.
9Yl8dL4yC9.main_concern: Comparisons with other methods are confounded by different generator training data, pretrained components (WebFace-21M, DINOv3), and recognition recipes, and the person-specific-variation claim is not uniquely established by the interventions.

g6XNseSGcn.one_liner: Unsupervised neural combinatorial optimization that moves exploration to training via self-improving population targets and decoder basin matching.
g6XNseSGcn.problem: Unsupervised NCO lacks supervisory signals; existing solvers compensate with iterative inference-time exploration, while direct inference is efficient but offers no exploration.
g6XNseSGcn.method: BOLT uses self-improving population guidance to progressively construct targets better than the current generator, and decoder basin matching to transfer these improvements back to the generator. Inference remains a single direct pass.
g6XNseSGcn.key_idea: Build improved target solution distributions from the generator's own sampled population, then match the decoder's output basin to them, moving exploration into training.
g6XNseSGcn.evidence: Experiments on three graph optimization problems (MIS, MaxCl, MDS per reviewers) at two graph scales against direct unsupervised NCO baselines, with ablations on target construction.
g6XNseSGcn.claimed_gains: Consistently improves solution quality over prior direct unsupervised NCO methods while retaining efficient inference; no numbers are stated in the abstract.
g6XNseSGcn.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the conceptual framing is clear and principled, and BOLT gives the lowest gap among direct-inference unsupervised baselines with fast inference.
g6XNseSGcn.main_concern: Results come from a single seed with ablation variants close to the full model, stronger non-direct NCO methods are not compared, and training cost and hyperparameters are missing.

JjKcmEQu4m.one_liner: Training-free editing projects RL weight updates onto the base model's leading spectral subspace, dropping orthogonal components.
JjKcmEQu4m.problem: Dense full-parameter RL updates suppress reasoning performance through premature saturation of test-time scaling and cause interference when consolidating multiple capabilities through multi-domain training or model merging.
JjKcmEQu4m.method: Subspace-Aligned Rewiring (SAR) is a post-hoc method that retains the part of the RL update concentrated in the base model's spectral space and removes orthogonal components, filtering residual directions that suppress performance or amplify cross-domain interference. It is used to extract reasoning cores, purify mixed-domain updates, and merge expert models.
JjKcmEQu4m.key_idea: Project the RL weight update onto the base model's leading singular subspaces and discard the orthogonal residual, which holds the suppressive and interfering directions.
JjKcmEQu4m.evidence: Several model families and scales (1.5B to 32B per reviewers), mathematical reasoning with Pass@k, agentic coding on an in-house model, mixed-domain purification, and model merging across experts.
JjKcmEQu4m.claimed_gains: Extracts compact reasoning cores using approximately 0.58% of total parameters while preserving over 99% of post-training performance, and improves six of seven open agentic coding benchmarks on an in-house model.
JjKcmEQu4m.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree SAR is a simple post-hoc method and that the finding that RL gains concentrate in the base model's spectral subspace is interesting, preserving performance across scales.
JjKcmEQu4m.main_concern: Novelty over prior work on sparse RL updates and geometry preservation is not distinguished, and gains are modest with evaluation on small benchmark sets such as AIME without variance.

3jggn4Fk9U.one_liner: Proves a ladder of dynamic-regret rates for streaming low-rank regression under abrupt coefficient jumps, with GLR change-point detection.
3jggn4Fk9U.problem: When the relevant subspace is fixed but coefficients jump abruptly, decaying steps recover slowly after jumps and constant steps keep a noise floor, a plasticity-stability tradeoff.
3jggn4Fk9U.method: The paper compares monotone decaying-step SGD, a clipped fixed-window estimator, and an adaptive estimator combining generalized likelihood ratio (GLR) change-point detection with clipped least squares, with a van Trees lower bound. For an unknown subspace, the detector runs on half of the samples projected onto a spectral-moment estimate built from the other half.
3jggn4Fk9U.key_idea: Combine GLR change-point detection with clipped least squares to reset the estimate at jumps, achieving O(sqrt(T) log T) regret that matches a van Trees lower bound.
3jggn4Fk9U.evidence: Theorems on expected dynamic regret under linear-Gaussian sample feedback with a matching lower bound; reviewers also cite experiments with separate test streams and detailed detection measurements.
3jggn4Fk9U.claimed_gains: Monotone decaying-step SGD has linear regret under jumps, a clipped fixed-window estimator achieves O(T^{3/4}) regret with sqrt(T) jumps, and the adaptive estimator achieves O(sqrt(T) log T) with a matching Omega(sqrt(T) log T) lower bound.
3jggn4Fk9U.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the matching regret rates, jump-size-resolved analysis, and clean problem formulation are useful and mathematically solid.
3jggn4Fk9U.main_concern: The main text packs in many theorems and technical terms with little narrative or discussion of how the results relate and what is novel in each, hurting readability.

MafOc3dJKT.one_liner: Input-anchored deep networks achieve absolute memorization in class-incremental learning by storing data moment tensors, instantiated as the Anchored MLP.
MafOc3dJKT.problem: Analytic class-incremental learning gives absolute memorization only for linear layers, and no prior work achieves it in deep neural networks.
MafOc3dJKT.method: The paper defines Input Anchoring and proves that degree-L networks with this property achieve absolute memorization with storage complexity O((d+1)^{2L}), identifies existing architectures with the property, and introduces the Anchored MLP (AMLP). The Loss-Anchoring Points (LAP) method approximates the stored statistics with polynomial storage and time.
MafOc3dJKT.key_idea: For input-anchored networks the full MSE loss is determined by data moment tensors, so storing them reproduces full replay without the original data.
MafOc3dJKT.evidence: A theorem on absolute memorization with storage complexity O((d+1)^{2L}) and experiments with AMLP and LAP; reviewers cite controls including a reproduced VILA baseline, increased random-feature width, and a gradient-trained linear head.
MafOc3dJKT.claimed_gains: Storage complexity O((d+1)^{2L}) for degree-L input-anchored networks, and LAP achieves the accuracy benefits of absolute memorization with polynomial storage and time; no accuracy numbers are stated.
MafOc3dJKT.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the input-anchoring formulation is a clear theoretical extension of analytic continual learning beyond linear heads, with AMLP showing how the theory applies.
MafOc3dJKT.main_concern: LAP's approximation quality and sensitivity to memory size are not evaluated, and the practical value of the deeper head over analytic linear heads on a frozen backbone is unclear.

7RT2dnY9fm.one_liner: Training-free zero-shot multi-label recognition with MLLMs: class-presence questions as isolated suffixes over a shared prefix, scored in one pass.
7RT2dnY9fm.problem: Generative MLLMs do not readily give a score for every candidate class in multi-label recognition, and evaluating class-specific questions separately repeats shared context computation.
7RT2dnY9fm.method: SPQ organizes class-presence questions as independent suffixes over a shared visual and instructional prefix, with block-isolated attention preventing information exchange between suffixes and aligned positional encodings preserving the context of standalone queries. It reads Yes/No logits at all class decision positions in a single joint forward pass.
7RT2dnY9fm.key_idea: Place all class-presence questions as attention-isolated suffixes with aligned positions over one shared prefix, and read Yes/No logits at every suffix in one forward pass.
7RT2dnY9fm.evidence: Four MLLM configurations spanning Qwen2.5-VL, LLaVA, and InternVL, with a direct comparison against independent binary querying and candidate-list generation.
7RT2dnY9fm.claimed_gains: Joint evaluation can preserve recognition performance relative to independent binary querying; the abstract states no numbers (a reviewer cites an 18.8x-27x speedup).
7RT2dnY9fm.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the method is straightforward and clearly written, with a large inference speedup over independent binary queries and good recognition performance.
7RT2dnY9fm.main_concern: Novelty is unclear relative to prior attention-masking and repeated-position-embedding work for multiple-choice options, and the speedup baseline is not a batched independent-query baseline.

6HhAPgHHF7.one_liner: Explains why momentum accelerates full-batch normalized steepest descent at the Edge of Stability by attenuating the alternating gradient component.
6HhAPgHHF7.problem: Existing analyses credit momentum in normalized steepest-descent optimizers to stochastic noise reduction and favor no momentum in deterministic training, yet full-batch training still benefits from momentum.
6HhAPgHHF7.method: At the Edge of Stability, normalization pins the effective learning rate at twice the inverse transverse curvature; momentum attenuates the alternating gradient component before normalization, raising the oscillation-onset threshold and multiplying post-onset progress by (1+beta)/(1-beta). A switched flow built from this mechanism predicts oscillation onset, subsequent speed, and the training loss.
6HhAPgHHF7.key_idea: Momentum averages out the alternating sharp-direction gradient before normalization, which delays oscillation onset and multiplies progress by (1+beta)/(1-beta) under normalized updates.
