gpo6UBSyJ6.evidence: Experiments compare uniform and competing weighting methods, vary verifiers and weighting models, and assess downstream reinforcement-learning policies.
gpo6UBSyJ6.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the rubric-weighting problem clear and the pairwise-comparison framework straightforward, with useful controlled weighting experiments.
gpo6UBSyJ6.main_concern: Quadratic comparison and revision costs lack sufficient justification against cheaper alternatives such as direct response-pair judgment.

Qn8nkXBro7.one_liner: Tracks template use and reasoning-function organization after matched supervised and reinforcement training for text-to-SQL generation.
Qn8nkXBro7.problem: It is unclear whether training on multiple reasoning templates produces useful strategy recombination beyond template imitation.
Qn8nkXBro7.method: The study balances four templates across matched training questions and compares supervised fine-tuning, rejection fine-tuning, and subsequent GRPO. Generated-response analysis and requested-template interventions track changes in expression and reasoning-function combinations.
Qn8nkXBro7.key_idea: Hold training questions and template coverage fixed, then measure how reinforcement learning changes reasoning-function combinations in generated SQL explanations.
Qn8nkXBro7.evidence: BIRD experiments use two 7B models, matched training paths, common decoding, and separate discovery and validation candidates.
Qn8nkXBro7.claimed_gains: RL changes reasoning-function combinations or order in 78.74% and 73.11% of identifiable same-question greedy responses for the two SFT models.
Qn8nkXBro7.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers praise the matched training comparisons, common evaluation rules, and controls that reduce selection bias.
Qn8nkXBro7.main_concern: Unvalidated reasoning-function detection cannot reliably distinguish genuine strategy reorganization from changes in wording, format, or template choice.

EmOOhXM37x.one_liner: Combines dual-stream speech modeling, character-conditioned fine-tuning, and interactive reinforcement learning for persona-consistent full-duplex dialogue.
EmOOhXM37x.problem: Full-duplex speech assistants need to maintain conversational character as well as real-time speaking and listening behavior.
EmOOhXM37x.method: CharDuplex adapts GLM-4-Voice to an always-on dual-stream architecture and fine-tunes on automatically generated character-conditioned dialogues. FDGym then trains the model through reinforcement learning with an LLM-simulated user in evolving multi-turn interactions.
EmOOhXM37x.key_idea: Train an always-on dual-stream speech model on persona-conditioned dialogue, then refine it through closed-loop interaction with a simulated user.
EmOOhXM37x.evidence: SpeechRole-Eval measures character consistency alongside evaluations of general speech intelligence and full-duplex interaction.
EmOOhXM37x.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers view the character-aware training pipeline as useful and acknowledge effective performance across speech, interaction, and persona evaluations.
EmOOhXM37x.main_concern: Small reinforcement-learning gains and missing matched controls leave FDGym's contribution beyond supervised training uncertain.

TQaXkmZ3sz.one_liner: Exchanges visual dynamics and 3D structure through a shared latent space while retaining separate video and motion generators.
TQaXkmZ3sz.problem: Direct attention between video and motion features struggles with mismatched spatial and temporal granularity in hand-object interaction generation.
TQaXkmZ3sz.method: UniHOI preserves modality-specific generation while constructing an intermediate latent representation for cross-modal exchange. The shared space organizes complementary visual dynamics and 3D structure, with geometric supervision anchoring the interaction.
TQaXkmZ3sz.key_idea: Mediate video-motion exchange through an interaction latent space organized around visual dynamics and 3D structure.
TQaXkmZ3sz.evidence: TACO experiments evaluate video generation, pose-controlled video generation, motion generation, component ablations, and an internal unseen-tool split.
TQaXkmZ3sz.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the granularity mismatch well motivated and the shared latent space a reasonable way to exchange visual and geometric information.
TQaXkmZ3sz.main_concern: All experiments use TACO, so an internal unseen-tool split does not establish broader cross-dataset generalization.

KWCymfx2aS.one_liner: Commits one high-probability interior EOS token at the first non-EOS step to redirect masked diffusion decoding.
KWCymfx2aS.problem: Irreversible early terminal-token commitments can steer masked diffusion models toward long, noncompliant answers despite suitable provisional predictions.
KWCymfx2aS.method: Shared-state branching isolates the effect of the first commitment, revealing that an interior EOS often triggers adjacent EOS commitments. EndFirst intervenes once on largely unpadded canvases by committing EOS at its highest-probability position, then restores the original decoder without extra forward passes.
KWCymfx2aS.key_idea: At the first non-EOS commitment step, write an interior EOS that induces adjacent padding before content generation.
KWCymfx2aS.evidence: Experiments use two LLaDA models on NQ and HotpotQA, with branching controls, held-out confirmation, and transfer checks across model families.
KWCymfx2aS.claimed_gains: Gated EndFirst improves exact match by 17.6–20.3 points, exceeds evaluation-set-selected every-step EOS bias by 4.7 points pooled, and raises judged-correct ten-word-compliant answers from roughly 17% to 46%.
KWCymfx2aS.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize substantial short-answer gains on LLaDA from a simple intervention requiring neither training nor extra forward passes.
KWCymfx2aS.main_concern: Evidence is concentrated on short-answer generation and tokenizer- or schedule-specific settings, leaving broader generation benefits uncertain.

dDmrGQ2GBj.one_liner: Aligns statistical specifications across tabular models to infer missing query features before retrieving compatible predictors.
dDmrGQ2GBj.problem: Incomplete individual queries may satisfy none of the feature requirements of reusable tabular models whose training data are unavailable.
dDmrGQ2GBj.method: The framework aligns model specifications along shared features into a query-dependent context. A pretrained tabular prior completes missing inputs, enabling model retrieval and prediction with model-specific completion uncertainty.
dDmrGQ2GBj.key_idea: Combine shared-feature relationships from different model specifications to complete a query before selecting tabular predictors.
dDmrGQ2GBj.evidence: Controlled fixed-predictor and specification-shuffling experiments use tabular model libraries constructed from benchmark subsets under MCAR and Group-MCAR missingness.
dDmrGQ2GBj.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value using other models' statistical specifications to support data-free reuse of heterogeneous tabular predictors.
dDmrGQ2GBj.main_concern: Libraries drawn from the same datasets with random feature masking insufficiently test independently developed models, conflicting distributions, and realistic missingness.

fAB2s4inFl.one_liner: Benchmarks image-to-HTML reconstruction through rendered-block alignment and human-calibrated judgments of visual fidelity.
fAB2s4inFl.problem: Document-to-HTML reconstruction lacks systematic evaluation of content, spatial structure, and rendered appearance across heterogeneous documents.
fAB2s4inFl.method: AmbiHTMLBench provides annotated document pages and an objective protocol that aligns rendered blocks to measure text, table, and layout fidelity. A reference-anchored subjective protocol uses language-model judges calibrated against human preferences.
fAB2s4inFl.key_idea: Evaluate reconstructed HTML through aligned rendered structures and a separate reference-anchored perceptual-fidelity protocol.
fAB2s4inFl.evidence: The benchmark includes 1,115 diverse pages, evaluates ten multimodal systems, and studies task-specific fine-tuning of a compact expert.
fAB2s4inFl.claimed_gains: The highest objective score among the evaluated systems is 0.8092.
fAB2s4inFl.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the practical HTML reconstruction task and complementary measurements of structural and perceived visual fidelity.
fAB2s4inFl.main_concern: An asymmetric preference estimator and unclear A/B assignment can bias subjective scores and model rankings.

giDkGo9omD.one_liner: Lean world models predict goal states and errors alongside proof steps, enabling diagnosis and repair within one response.
giDkGo9omD.problem: Open-loop theorem provers can derail after incorrect assumptions about proof state and often rely on reasoning distilled from expensive teachers.
giDkGo9omD.method: Qwen3 provers learn to generate Lean goal states and error messages alongside proof steps through feedback-annotated supervised training followed by GRPO. Predicted diagnostics support repairing failed proofs within the same response without intermediate verifier calls.
giDkGo9omD.key_idea: Supervising predicted Lean states and error messages lets the prover use its own diagnostics for within-response proof repair.
giDkGo9omD.evidence: Experiments train 4B and 8B Qwen3 models on miniF2F and ProofNet, comparing standard provers, informal-reasoning variants, repair behavior, and feedback accuracy.
giDkGo9omD.claimed_gains: The 8B world-model prover reaches 75.61% pass@32 on miniF2F and 16.44% on ProofNet versus 71.31% and 13.21%, and adding informal reasoning raises miniF2F pass@32 to 77.05%.
giDkGo9omD.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find predicted diagnostics and within-response repair useful extensions of proof-state prediction and acknowledge substantial training and experimental work.
giDkGo9omD.main_concern: Baseline differences in replay, feedback supervision, and training data prevent clean attribution of gains to feedback prediction.

ka2leC87HL.one_liner: Conditions an online contrastive RL actor on relative direction and distance to visited waypoints in critic-embedding space.
ka2leC87HL.problem: Online Contrastive Reinforcement Learning trains policies on raw goal coordinates, failing to directly exploit the reachability geometry learned by its critic encoder.
ka2leC87HL.method: Direction-Conditioned Policies (DCP) modifies online Contrastive RL by selecting visited states as training waypoints and conditioning the actor on the normalized direction and distance to those targets inside the critic's learned representation space. At deployment, the actor queries the final goal through the same directional representation interface without waypoint selection or planning.
ka2leC87HL.key_idea: Condition the online Contrastive RL policy on relative direction and distance in the critic's representation space using visited-state waypoints during training.
ka2leC87HL.evidence: Evaluated across nine simulated navigation and manipulation tasks (five seeds) plus controlled maze shortest-path geometry and causal direction-steering ablations.
ka2leC87HL.claimed_gains: Across nine navigation and manipulation tasks, DCP attains higher final success rates than CRL on seven tasks and spends more time near the goal on seven.
ka2leC87HL.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that modifying only the actor's input interface to consume critic-space direction and distance is simple, incurs minimal runtime overhead, and yields consistent multi-seed gains.
ka2leC87HL.main_concern: Reviewers note that the nine-task benchmark omits a direct-goal direction-conditioned variant without waypoint scoring—even though controlled maze ablations show waypoint scoring can hurt—leaving the two changes confounded.

f4AzKkCGvX.one_liner: Distills a risk-minimizing convex mixture of parametric and retrieval-conditioned teacher distributions to train retrieval-robust student LLMs.
f4AzKkCGvX.problem: Directly distilling a teacher LLM's retrieval-conditioned predictions propagates errors into smaller student models whenever retrieved passages are noisy or misleading.
f4AzKkCGvX.method: Mixture RAG-KD trains student models on a convex combination (1 - alpha)p + alpha*p_c of the teacher's parametric distribution and retrieval-conditioned distribution. Grounded in a target-risk analysis showing intermediate mixtures can achieve lower risk than either endpoint, it selects global or instance-wise mixing weights alpha by minimizing forward-KL or squared-L2 risk.
f4AzKkCGvX.key_idea: Interpolate a teacher LLM's parametric and retrieval-conditioned output distributions using global or instance-wise weights chosen by forward-KL or squared-L2 risk minimization.
f4AzKkCGvX.evidence: Supported by target-risk optimality analysis and distillation experiments within the Gemma-3 family (12B teacher to 1B and 4B students) on general QA (Natural Questions) and noisy-retrieval settings.
f4AzKkCGvX.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that retrieval both fixes and corrupts parametric teacher predictions, making lightweight cached-logit interpolation between parametric and RAG teacher distributions intuitive and practical.
f4AzKkCGvX.main_concern: Reviewers point to limited methodological originality over standard ensemble logit interpolation, small-scale Gemma-3-only experiments (1,000 NQ training examples), and lack of direct evaluation of the un-distilled teacher mixture.

A3bMBp8vfy.one_liner: Merges independent audio and visual teacher reasoning traces via an LLM for SFT cold-start before multimodal RL.
A3bMBp8vfy.problem: Training audio-visual reasoning models is bottlenecked by scarce high-quality cross-modal reasoning traces and the lack of strong native audio-visual teacher models.
A3bMBp8vfy.method: AVRT generates separate audio and visual reasoning traces using specialized single-modality teacher models and combines them into unified cross-modal reasoning traces via a prompted LLM merger. These synthetic traces initialize the target multimodal model in a supervised fine-tuning cold-start stage prior to larger-scale reinforcement learning (GRPO).
A3bMBp8vfy.key_idea: Fuse independent audio-teacher and visual-teacher reasoning traces with an LLM merger to supervised-fine-tune an audio-visual model before reinforcement learning.
A3bMBp8vfy.evidence: Evaluated at 3B and 7B model scales (using 20K SFT samples followed by GRPO) across audio-visual reasoning benchmarks including OmniBench and DailyOmni against RL-only baselines.
A3bMBp8vfy.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that merging separate single-modality teacher traces avoids needing a native audio-visual teacher and achieves strong data-efficient improvements across 3B and 7B models.
A3bMBp8vfy.main_concern: Reviewers note limited algorithmic originality in prompt-based trace merging and missing SFT-only and naive trace-concatenation ablations needed to isolate cross-modal composition and the data-heavy RL stage.

b2X3AhIc7h.one_liner: Expands prompt trees via position-debiased pairwise LLM comparisons and selects prompts through Bayesian path filtering and BTL tournaments.
b2X3AhIc7h.problem: Agentic tree-search prompt optimizers rely on ground-truth supervision rewards, whereas unsupervised local pairwise LLM comparisons lack a consistent global quality scale.
b2X3AhIc7h.method: Unsupervised Prompt Agent (UPA) explores structured prompt spaces by iteratively growing a search tree guided by position-debiased pairwise LLM comparisons without ground-truth labels. To obtain a globally consistent selection, a two-stage Bradley-Terry-Luce (BTL) procedure applies path-wise Bayesian aggregation to filter candidates under uncertainty, followed by a global tournament to infer latent prompt quality.
b2X3AhIc7h.key_idea: Decouple reward-free prompt tree exploration via position-debiased pairwise LLM judgments from two-stage Bradley-Terry-Luce selection combining path-wise Bayesian filtering and global tournaments.
b2X3AhIc7h.evidence: Evaluated across five closed-ended and open-ended prompt-optimization benchmarks under matched search budgets against ground-truth-free baselines (including SPO and PDO) and alternative tree search organizations.
b2X3AhIc7h.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the two-stage unsupervised search-and-selection procedure is clearly specified, reproducible, and thoroughly tested across closed-ended and open-ended benchmarks with matched-budget search ablations.
b2X3AhIc7h.main_concern: Reviewers question the statistical significance of small gains over ground-truth-free baselines without confidence intervals, unverified reliability of pairwise LLM prompt judging, and omission of DEEVO.

QloJ5LvN1r.one_liner: Stores historical target logits with prefix contexts and scores cross-prefix transferability to orchestrate speculative draft trees.
QloJ5LvN1r.problem: Token-recycling speculative decoding methods assume historical target-model predictions remain valid whenever a token recurs, wasting verification budget when predictions fail to transfer across divergent prefixes.
QloJ5LvN1r.method: RECAP maintains a multi-context verification memory pairing recycled target-model logits with their originating prefix contexts, and runs a lightweight learned prefix-conditioned scorer to estimate candidate transferability under the current prefix. These calibrated reliability scores jointly govern candidate selection and verification-budget allocation during adaptive draft-tree construction.
QloJ5LvN1r.key_idea: Score cross-prefix transferability of cached target-model logits from a multi-context verification memory to allocate candidate slots in speculative draft trees.
QloJ5LvN1r.evidence: Evaluated across multiple target LLMs and speculative decoding benchmarks with ablations on memory scoring and adaptive tree orchestration.
QloJ5LvN1r.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that conditioning historical token-logit reuse on prefix context rather than token identity alone addresses a clear transferability bottleneck and improves draft acceptance lengths.
QloJ5LvN1r.main_concern: Reviewers note considerable per-round scorer and orchestration overhead that tempers end-to-end wall-clock speedups (evaluated mainly at batch size 1 and greedy decoding) and incremental scope over prior tree drafters.

7MiJeIFRpV.one_liner: Crosses behavioral form adherence with intent alignment in news-grounded cultural narratives to test LLM value-judgment blind spots.
7MiJeIFRpV.problem: LLMs evaluating social and cultural behavior can mistake outward adherence to expected behavioral form for genuine alignment with the underlying value.
7MiJeIFRpV.method: FACADE operationalizes form-value divergence via a 2x2 Behavior-Value matrix crossing Behavior Adherence and Value Alignment into Full Compliance, Principled Compliance, Surface Compliance, and Non-Compliance. Using a news-augmented story generation pipeline grounded in real-world event patterns and cultural norms, it constructs matched narrative contrasts to test whether LLMs reject performative surface compliance.
7MiJeIFRpV.key_idea: Independently manipulate outward behavioral adherence and underlying social intent across news-grounded cultural narratives to test LLM detection of performative surface compliance.
7MiJeIFRpV.evidence: Evaluated 20 LLMs on 9,416 news-augmented stories derived from 2,354 source norms spanning 75 countries and regions with human comparability and verification checks.
7MiJeIFRpV.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the four-quadrant Behavior-Value matrix provides diagnostically informative matched contrasts across 75 regions and exposes a clear LLM blind spot on surface-compliant value violations.
7MiJeIFRpV.main_concern: Reviewers note that models judge stories without seeing the authors' extracted underlying value—conflating cultural appropriateness with inferring intended labels—and that surface-compliance drops may reflect higher reasoning complexity.

TxbAtwVes7.one_liner: Decomposes panoramas into calibrated perspective sub-views, predicts poses with a 3D foundation model, and performs Cauchy-Bayesian fusion.
TxbAtwVes7.problem: Conventional pixel-matching and RANSAC panoramic registration fails under extreme low overlap and visual ambiguity where reliable point correspondences are scarce.
TxbAtwVes7.method: PanoREG decomposes each panorama into calibrated perspective sub-views, predicts cross-view relative poses with a frozen 3D foundation model, and maps them through known sub-view-to-panorama extrinsics into multiple noisy panorama-level pose hypotheses. It then models hypothesis residuals with an outlier-robust Cauchy likelihood and performs Bayesian inference to recover the maximum a posteriori panorama pose without task-specific training.
TxbAtwVes7.key_idea: Generate panorama-level relative pose hypotheses from frozen 3D foundation-model predictions on calibrated perspective sub-views and fuse them via Cauchy-likelihood Bayesian MAP estimation.
TxbAtwVes7.evidence: Evaluated training-free across indoor panoramic registration benchmarks including Stanford2D3D, Matterport3D, and PanoCity, particularly in low-overlap regimes.
TxbAtwVes7.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that leveraging a frozen 3D foundation model over calibrated perspective sub-views with geometric consistency weighting achieves strong training-free accuracy and fast (~2 s) runtime under low overlap.
TxbAtwVes7.main_concern: Reviewers question whether gains stem mainly from VGGT or PanoVGGT's multi-view reasoning rather than Bayesian fusion, note missing comparisons to direct rig bundle adjustment, and highlight indoor-only dataset evaluation.

REROni49jT.one_liner: Expands VLM vocabularies with single-token atomic glyph units initialized from constituent subwords for generative OCR fine-tuning.
REROni49jT.problem: In generative VLM-based OCR, visually atomic rare or historical glyphs fragment into multi-token byte or subword sequences, causing autoregressive error propagation.
REROni49jT.method: Glyph-Aligned Output-Space Adaptation (GAOSA) replaces fragmented multi-token character encodings with single atomic character-level output tokens initialized from their constituent subword representations, then jointly adapts token embeddings and the language-modeling head under transcription supervision. For full-page OCR, it also synthesizes target characters into historical page layouts for joint layout-and-transcription training.
REROni49jT.key_idea: Collapse fragmented multi-token glyphs into constituent-initialized single character tokens and jointly fine-tune VLM input embeddings and output heads on transcriptions.
REROni49jT.evidence: Evaluated primarily on historical Chinese character and full-page OCR alongside Ethiopic and IPA scripts across VLM backbones against standard SFT.
REROni49jT.claimed_gains: In historical Chinese OCR, standard SFT improves target character F1 from 7.6% to 59.7%, while GAOSA further raises it to 88.6%.
REROni49jT.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that eliminating multi-token glyph fragmentation yields large, well-controlled F1 improvements (+28.87 percentage points) over matched-data SFT across historical Chinese and low-resource scripts.
REROni49jT.main_concern: Reviewers note limited methodological originality over prior vocabulary-expansion OCR work (such as TongGuOCR), missing comparisons against non-generative traditional OCR pipelines, and unanalyzed vocabulary-scaling trade-offs.

xv24LMS9qX.one_liner: Formalizes observed Transformer information-propagation rules to prove single-pass asymptotic step bounds and construct depth-optimal symbolic reasoners.
xv24LMS9qX.problem: The intrinsic multi-step reasoning depth achievable by an L-layer Transformer in a single forward pass and its dependence on premise ordering remain theoretically underspecified.
xv24LMS9qX.method: Motivated by attention propagation patterns observed in Transformers trained on symbolic multi-step deduction chains, the authors formalize discrete information-propagation rules under causal masking. They derive upper and lower bounds on single-pass reasoning depth as a function of layer count L, characterize favorable interleaved fact orderings, and explicitly construct a Transformer achieving the upper bound.
xv24LMS9qX.key_idea: Model single-pass symbolic chain deduction via empirically observed causal information-propagation rules to bound L-layer reasoning depth and identify layer-efficient interleaved premise orderings.
xv24LMS9qX.evidence: Supported by formal upper and lower depth proofs, an explicit constructive Transformer weight implementation, and empirical premise-ordering experiments on three-layer models solving four-hop symbolic chains.
xv24LMS9qX.claimed_gains: Under the proposed propagation rules, an L-layer Transformer's single-pass reasoning limit lies between 2^(L-1) - 1 and (3^(L-1) - 1) / 2 steps, and this limiting depth is constructively achievable.
xv24LMS9qX.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that predicting and empirically confirming higher three-layer accuracy on interleaved rather than natural logical premise orderings provides a sharp, counterintuitive link between theory and experiment.
xv24LMS9qX.main_concern: Reviewers point out that the upper bound holds only conditionally under the prescribed propagation rules rather than bounding unrestricted Transformer computations, while empirical depth and step sweeps remain narrow.

QeGW2SC1I1.one_liner: Re-runs a frozen audio encoder tail conditioned on intermediate LLM hidden states via a shared low-rank cell.
QeGW2SC1I1.problem: Standard one-pass audio-language models finish acoustic encoding before language decoding begins, preventing evolving intermediate language representations from guiding further acoustic processing.
QeGW2SC1I1.method: AuralLoop uses a shared low-rank cell to condition a cached intermediate acoustic anchor on an evolving language-model hidden state, reruns the frozen audio encoder tail, and injects the resulting embedding deltas into audio-token positions at later LLM layers. Two iterative re-entry steps share the cached anchor, low-rank cell, and frozen backbone weights.
QeGW2SC1I1.key_idea: Condition a cached acoustic anchor on intermediate LLM hidden states via a shared low-rank cell, rerun the frozen audio-encoder tail, and inject deltas.
QeGW2SC1I1.evidence: Instantiated on frozen Qwen2.5-Omni-7B (3.20M trainable parameters) and evaluated across ADQA, VoxParadox, MMSU, and MUGEN against static features, single-call re-entry, and compute-matched joint audio-language LoRA.
QeGW2SC1I1.claimed_gains: On Qwen2.5-Omni-7B with 3.20M trainable parameters, AuralLoop improves VoxParadox mean accuracy by 1.10 percentage points over single late-layer re-entry and by 0.97 points over joint audio-language LoRA under a controlled training-work budget.
QeGW2SC1I1.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that language-guided re-entry into a frozen audio encoder is parameter-efficient and evaluated with careful compute-matched and conditioning-intervention controls.
QeGW2SC1I1.main_concern: Reviewers note that accuracy gains over joint LoRA are small (0.29-0.97 points) relative to architectural complexity and 19-23% higher time-to-first-token, tested only on Qwen2.5-Omni-7B multiple-choice tasks without population confidence intervals.

3lIONcNrDu.one_liner: Combines cross-loop activation canonicalization, interaction-aware loop bit allocation, and recursive trajectory calibration to quantize looped Transformers.
3lIONcNrDu.problem: Standard post-training quantization designed for feed-forward Transformers degrades sharply on Looped Language Models due to shifting cross-loop activation distributions, heterogeneous loop sensitivities, and recursive error accumulation.
3lIONcNrDu.method: LoopQuant combines three post-training quantization stages for shared-weight looped Transformers: Cross-Loop Distribution Canonicalization (CLDC) to align recurrent-state distributions while preserving weight sharing, Interaction-Aware Loop-wise Precision Allocation (ILPA) to assign per-loop activation bits under cross-loop error interactions, and Loop-Conditioned Task Calibration (LCTC) to align quantized execution with the low-bit recursive trajectory.
3lIONcNrDu.key_idea: Canonicalize recurrent activation distributions across shared-weight loops, allocate loop-wise activation bit-widths using cross-loop interaction sensitivity, and calibrate against low-bit recursive trajectories.
3lIONcNrDu.evidence: Supported by a second-order task-loss decomposition and evaluated under W4A4 and W4A6 against W4A8 PTQ baselines across Ouro-2.6B, Nanbeige, and Huginn on language modeling, MMLU, GSM8K, and HumanEval.
3lIONcNrDu.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that decomposing loop-local sensitivity and cross-loop trajectory error provides a principled, coherent PTQ design that achieves strong W4A4 and W4A6 accuracy across multiple LoopLMs.
3lIONcNrDu.main_concern: Reviewers highlight the absence of a same-budget LoopQuant-W4A8 baseline to isolate gains from bit-width differences, un-reproduced comparisons against LoopQ, and inconsistent storage and speedup reporting.

cZ3tTBvIUH.one_liner: Evaluates classical, neural, and foundation-model causal discovery under a shared protocol across synthetic, semantic, formula, and real SCMs.
cZ3tTBvIUH.problem: Disparate synthetic structural causal model protocols and pretraining-test distribution overlap obscure whether causal discovery foundation models genuinely generalize beyond their training generators.
cZ3tTBvIUH.method: CausalArena unifies causal discovery evaluation under shared observational and interventional interfaces across four regimes: synthetic SCMs, LLM-assisted human-auditable semantic operational SCMs, formula-grounded scientific SCMs, and public real-world datasets. Using an evolvable generation pipeline, it tests how method rankings shift across structural and mechanistic regimes.
cZ3tTBvIUH.key_idea: Benchmark causal discovery methods under unified observational and interventional interfaces spanning synthetic, LLM-grounded semantic, scientific-formula, and real-world structural causal models.
cZ3tTBvIUH.evidence: Evaluates 18 classical, neural, and foundation-model causal discovery methods across 1,200 executable SCMs (1,000 synthetic, 100 semantic operational, and 100 formula-grounded scientific) plus public real-world datasets.
cZ3tTBvIUH.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that assembling 1,200 executable synthetic, semantic, and scientific SCMs under shared observational and interventional interfaces provides practical value for testing causal discovery generalization across 18 methods.
cZ3tTBvIUH.main_concern: Reviewers note that pretrained models remain trained on disparate uncontrolled datasets, while the LLM-based semantic simulator pipeline is under-explained in the main text and cross-family aggregations and tables lack clarity.

ydtrHbIcrw.one_liner: Training-free recurrent video token compressor selecting anchors via Maximum Mean Discrepancy to complement the preceding frame's state.
ydtrHbIcrw.problem: Independent frame-wise visual token compressors repeatedly retain redundant content across frames while missing newly unfolding video information.
ydtrHbIcrw.method: C²V uses the preceding frame's compressed representation as a recurrent visual state and greedily selects current-frame anchor tokens minimizing Maximum Mean Discrepancy between the attention-weighted scene distribution and an optimal convex mixture of the state and candidate anchors. Mass-preserving aggregation folds unselected tokens' features and probability mass into the anchors to produce LLM inputs and the next visual state.
ydtrHbIcrw.key_idea: Greedily select current-frame token anchors minimizing Maximum Mean Discrepancy as a convex mixture with the prior frame's compressed state, followed by mass-preserving feature aggregation.
ydtrHbIcrw.evidence: Evaluated across five short-to-long video benchmarks using Qwen3-VL-8B, InternVideo3-8B, and Qwen2.5-VL-7B at four token retention ratios (10–25%).
ydtrHbIcrw.claimed_gains: Achieves the highest five-benchmark average accuracy among evaluated compressors across all 12 model and retention-ratio (10–25%) configurations.
ydtrHbIcrw.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers commend the principled distribution-matching formulation with closed-form mixture weights and consistent accuracy across models and retention budgets.
ydtrHbIcrw.main_concern: Storing only the immediately preceding frame's state may not prevent long-range redundancy when scenes recur, recurrence yields a modest ablation margin, and differences from prior stateful video pruners need clearer isolation.

dOp4LzPkIU.one_liner: Combines vector-scalar geometric message passing with bidirectional residue-atom alignment for 3D enzyme-substrate specificity prediction and residue attribution.
dOp4LzPkIU.problem: Computational enzyme-substrate specificity predictors provide limited modeling of pair-specific 3D directional residue-substrate interactions needed for recognition and residue prioritization.
dOp4LzPkIU.method: StereoVSE integrates protein sequence representations, molecular graph features, and 3D enzyme-substrate structural complexes through a Vector-Scalar graph neural network and Bidirectional Residue-Atom Interaction Alignment. The learned substrate-conditioned interaction signals support both specificity classification and active-site candidate residue prioritization.
dOp4LzPkIU.key_idea: Integrate protein sequence, molecular features, and 3D complex structures via vector-scalar message passing and bidirectional residue-atom alignment for substrate-conditioned specificity and residue attribution.
dOp4LzPkIU.evidence: Evaluated on halogenase and glycosyltransferase specificity benchmarks (including cold-start halogenase splits and module ablations per reviews) alongside residue-attribution analyses.
dOp4LzPkIU.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that combining sequence, chemical, and 3D structural representations yields consistent gains on halogenase and glycosyltransferase benchmarks backed by module ablations.
dOp4LzPkIU.main_concern: Despite framing around stereochemistry, reflection-invariant geometric operations are never tested on controlled stereoisomer pairs, cold-start splits do not exclude close homologs or scaffolds, and pretrained-encoder gains are not fully isolated.

xTF8HImtul.one_liner: Gates a differentiable terrain-elevation wet/dry water-level branch with neural surrogate predictions for few-shot regional coastal flood transfer.
xTF8HImtul.problem: Transferring deep-learning coastal flood surrogates to new regions requires generating many computationally expensive hydrodynamic simulations for target-region fine-tuning.
xTF8HImtul.method: The Physics Adapter (PA) is a compact, architecture-agnostic interface that predicts peak water level through a differentiable wet/dry response comparing terrain elevation against a learned water level and blends it with a data-driven surrogate branch via a learned gate. It embeds elevation as an architectural inductive bias without PDE-residual losses and pairs with parameter-efficient fine-tuning.
xTF8HImtul.key_idea: Blend a differentiable terrain-elevation-versus-learned-water-level wet/dry response with neural surrogate outputs via a learned gate for lightweight few-shot flood model adaptation.
xTF8HImtul.evidence: Integrated into 12 heterogeneous backbones (graph, convolutional, Transformer, state-space, depth-foundation, and diffusion models) and evaluated in Abu Dhabi, San Francisco, and Dubai against full fine-tuning and PEFT baselines.
xTF8HImtul.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the lightweight elevation-guided adapter intuitive, clearly written, and convincingly model-agnostic across 12 diverse neural backbones.
xTF8HImtul.main_concern: Reviewers view gating a known static inundation rule with surrogate outputs as methodologically incremental, note missing main-text component ablations, and question regional transferability claims given limited test regions and missing flood-detection metrics.

Y6guuQPMc0.one_liner: Renders calibrated camera poses as appearance-free corridor videos to guide four-step RL-refined video diffusion along prescribed UAV flights.
Y6guuQPMc0.problem: Pretrained video models either drift from geometric camera instructions or leak source appearance and geometry when generating visually distinct scenes along a prescribed flight trajectory.
Y6guuQPMc0.method: WorldSlider introduces FlightGrid, rendering calibrated camera poses into an appearance-free control video of the trajectory and surrounding flight corridor, and distills the generator to four inference steps. It further refines trajectory alignment via reinforcement learning using feedback from a camera-motion verifier to synthesize diverse training data for UAV visuomotor policies.
Y6guuQPMc0.key_idea: Render calibrated flight poses into an appearance-free corridor control video (FlightGrid) and refine a four-step distilled video diffusion model with camera-motion verifier RL.
Y6guuQPMc0.evidence: Evaluated on standard and diverse UAV flight trajectories, simulated-to-real qualitative transfers, and simulated visuomotor UAV policy training (adapted on 26 hours of flight footage at 10 FPS per TL;DR).
Y6guuQPMc0.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that FlightGrid is a simple, effective pose-to-video control representation that outperforms analytic camera encodings such as Plücker rays and PRoPE on coupled flight motion.
Y6guuQPMc0.main_concern: Reviewers note that parallel-world flight generation overlaps standard camera-controlled video generation, baseline Plücker/PRoPE controls use LoRA rather than FlightGrid's ControlNet branch without matched parameter reporting, and RL relies on a monocular pose estimator.

251iaLJZaS.one_liner: Transiently gates each tensor's momentum contribution by gradient-momentum alignment without modifying optimizer state or adding hyperparameters.
251iaLJZaS.problem: Changing local loss geometry and mini-batch noise frequently misalign accumulated optimizer momentum with the current gradient direction.
251iaLJZaS.method: AGAM is a hyperparameter-free, two-line drop-in modification for SGDM, AdamW, and Lion that transiently scales historical momentum's contribution in the update via a tensor-wise alignment-adaptive gating coefficient while keeping the stored momentum buffer unchanged. The paper characterizes AGAM's exact link to quasi-hyperbolic optimization and proves a sharp descent certificate for AGAM-SGD.
251iaLJZaS.key_idea: Transiently attenuate historical momentum per tensor in the parameter update according to current gradient-momentum alignment while preserving stored momentum state without new hyperparameters.
251iaLJZaS.evidence: Theoretical relation to quasi-hyperbolic optimization and sharp descent certificate for AGAM-SGD, plus experiments across ResNet classification, MAE ViT pre-training, and LLM fine-tuning with SGDM, AdamW, and Lion.
251iaLJZaS.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers praise AGAM's hyperparameter-free, state-preserving two-line design and systematic evaluation across SGDM, AdamW, and Lion over learning-rate and batch-size grids.
251iaLJZaS.main_concern: Reviewers note AGAM closely resembles quasi-hyperbolic momentum (QHM/QHAdam) and related gradient-momentum mixing updates, and lacks tuned fixed-gate QHM controls to isolate the benefit of alignment-dependent gating.

Jm5TXsIank.one_liner: Uses k-FWL algebra to separate structural distinctions missing from finite graph encodings versus distinctions lost during readout pooling.
Jm5TXsIank.problem: Asymptotic Weisfeiler-Leman expressivity bounds do not determine whether a finite-budget graph structural encoding fails because features lack information or because pooling erases it.
Jm5TXsIank.method: Using k-dimensional folklore Weisfeiler-Leman (k ≥ 2) algebra as a reference, the authors compare walk, endpoint, and joint encodings across polynomial degrees, channel budgets, object domains, and readouts. They verify feature-versus-readout mechanisms via exact algebraic checks—including invertible channel mixing before cubing and averaging—and matched-width pair, node, and edge experiments.
Jm5TXsIank.key_idea: Analyze finite walk, endpoint, and joint graph encodings in k-FWL algebra to distinguish missing feature-level distinctions from information erased by channelwise readout pooling.
Jm5TXsIank.evidence: Algebraic proofs and exact separation checks on strongly regular graphs (four-clique-count pairs and rook/Shrikhande graphs) alongside matched-width pair, node, and edge prediction experiments.
Jm5TXsIank.claimed_gains: Establishes exact degree-one separation of matching-parameter strongly regular graphs with different four-clique counts via joint augmentation at equal channel width, and degree-one rook/Shrikhande separation via invertible mixing before cubing and averaging without extra channels.
Jm5TXsIank.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value explicitly separating which distinctions are generated by finite encoding operations from which distinctions survive pooling readouts across graph object domains.
Jm5TXsIank.main_concern: Reviewers find the notation dense and question theorem-level novelty beyond prior polynomial, matrix, and tensor-language characterizations of higher-order WL (such as Maron et al. and Geerts and Reutter).

Gy9946NP7W.one_liner: Learns a conditional generative inverse that creates target-style adaptation signals for source-free sequence regression.
Gy9946NP7W.problem: Classification-oriented source-free adaptation relies on discrete clusters and pseudo-labels that do not transfer naturally to continuous sequence regression.
Gy9946NP7W.method: GIRA defines generalized classes over continuous outputs and trains a conditional generator to invert the pretrained regressor and produce target-style inputs. Generated input-class pairs adapt the regressor, with uncertainty filtering and feature-scale constraints limiting negative transfer.
Gy9946NP7W.key_idea: Generate target-style inputs conditioned on generalized continuous-output classes and use those synthetic pairs as source-free regression adaptation signals.
Gy9946NP7W.evidence: Experiments cover nine transfer scenarios across three sequence-regression tasks, with comparisons against zero-shot and other adaptation methods and component ablations.
Gy9946NP7W.claimed_gains: GIRA reduces MAE by 20.87% on average relative to zero-shot across nine transfer scenarios.
Gy9946NP7W.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that source-free sequence regression is meaningful and underexplored and that a learned inverse provides an interesting adaptation signal across continuous outputs.
Gy9946NP7W.main_concern: Reviewers consistently question whether adaptation corrects target errors or merely reinforces the source model’s potentially biased predictions used as fixed targets.

0AKyAPlwBm.one_liner: Benchmarks whether agents can investigate vulnerability reports and issue evidence-grounded accept-or-reject verdicts.
0AKyAPlwBm.problem: Existing vulnerability benchmarks evaluate detection or exploitation of confirmed flaws rather than whether submitted reports should be upheld.
0AKyAPlwBm.method: VulVerifyBench gives agents scrubbed reports and, where available, repositories for independent investigation and evidence-supported verdicts. It includes invalid reports, behavioral hard negatives, and counterfactual negatives pairing unchanged reports with patched code.
0AKyAPlwBm.key_idea: Evaluate report verification separately from reproduction by including claims whose observed behavior does not justify acceptance and patched-code counterfactuals with constructed labels.
0AKyAPlwBm.evidence: The benchmark contains 747 reports across smart contracts, traditional software, and web applications, including 220 invalid reports, 45 hard negatives, and 88 counterfactual negatives, evaluated with four backends.
0AKyAPlwBm.claimed_gains: The best domain accuracies are 84.5%, 87.5%, and 78.4%, but no backend exceeds 77.8% recall on hard negatives.
0AKyAPlwBm.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that report verification is an important and complementary benchmark task and that rejected and counterfactual reports expose failures beyond successful reproduction.
0AKyAPlwBm.main_concern: Reviewers question the robustness of conclusions drawn from only 45 potentially noisy hard negatives and the absence of a report-only investigation control.

5ZKJDrkw0s.one_liner: Uses target failures to diagnose and selectively repair causal policy shortcuts through source-simulator interventions.
5ZKJDrkw0s.problem: Visual control policies can fail after deployment through hidden nuisance dependence that observational source data cannot identify or safely repair.
5ZKJDrkw0s.method: RENDER reenacts candidate nuisance mechanisms in the source simulator to reproduce a few unpaired target failures, then tests task-preserving interventions for changes in decisions and task loss. Verified mechanisms guide adaptor training while the policy stays frozen; otherwise, RENDER abstains.
5ZKJDrkw0s.key_idea: Select source interventions by their ability to reproduce target failures and causally alter policy decisions before repairing only the implicated dependence.
5ZKJDrkw0s.evidence: Experiments span ForkRoad, Atari, CARLA, and other visual-control settings, with causal diagnosis, selective repair, source-performance preservation, and ablation analyses.
5ZKJDrkw0s.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the deployment setting is practical and that separating which dependencies exist from which one caused the observed failure is useful.
5ZKJDrkw0s.main_concern: Reviewers most often question reliance on a predefined intervention library and a simulator that can reproduce the responsible deployment shift, with limited complex real-world validation.

EE1r2gFfaD.one_liner: Learns positive-definite transport mobility from optimal-transport velocities while keeping the energy-defined target density fixed.
EE1r2gFfaD.problem: Energy Matching ties density and transport to one scalar energy, so changing the energy to improve movement also changes the sampled distribution.
EE1r2gFfaD.method: REM learns a symmetric positive-definite mobility that redirects a frozen energy gradient under a unit-determinant constraint. An objective fits optimal-transport velocities, and a divergence correction makes the resulting diffusion preserve the Boltzmann density.
EE1r2gFfaD.key_idea: Learn a unit-determinant Riemannian mobility that redirects frozen energy gradients along transport paths, with divergence correction preserving the original density.
EE1r2gFfaD.evidence: Experiments include a curved multimodal target, a high-dimensional field-fitting study, correction ablations, and image generation using deterministic learned geometry followed by Euclidean stochastic refinement.
EE1r2gFfaD.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that separating transport geometry from density learning is clean and well motivated and that fixed-density mobility is an appealing idea.
EE1r2gFfaD.main_concern: Reviewers most often note that the image gains do not use the central corrected stochastic mechanism throughout sampling and remain modest relative to added complexity.

gLC6IadYnz.one_liner: Uses a frozen hidden-state commitment probe to penalize only post-commitment tokens during RL and stop CoT early at inference.
gLC6IadYnz.problem: Uniform length penalties in reasoning RL compress necessary early reasoning alongside redundant post-answer text, hurting accuracy on hard problems.
gLC6IadYnz.method: CAP reads a frozen linear commitment probe from hidden states during GRPO forward passes and applies length penalties only to tokens generated after internal answer commitment. At inference, the same probe acts as an early-stopping rule based on commitment streaks.
gLC6IadYnz.key_idea: Reads a frozen hidden-state commitment probe during GRPO to penalize only post-commitment tokens and trigger early stopping at inference.
gLC6IadYnz.evidence: Full-scale RL on Qwen3-8B across MMLU-Pro, MATH-500, AIME 2025, GPQA-Diamond, and ZebraLogic, plus causal forced-decoding ablations.
gLC6IadYnz.claimed_gains: On Qwen3-8B, CAP matches outcome-only GRPO accuracy (+0.1 points, 95% CI [-1.8, +2.0]) with 9-28% fewer tokens, removes 47% of post-commitment text while length penalties trail by 8.7 and 10.6 points on MMLU-Pro, and at inference removes 54.9% of CoT tokens on MATH-500 for 2.7 points.
gLC6IadYnz.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that targeting post-commitment reasoning rather than global CoT length is intuitive, practical, and well-validated on Qwen3-8B.
gLC6IadYnz.main_concern: Reviewers note that commitment probes are fragile across model families (failing on Llama-8B) and drift during RL, alongside limited novelty over prior commitment-probe works.

x9ONyY0iRS.one_liner: Measures order-learnability across 21 factorization orders and 12 corpora using Transformer prequential codelength.
x9ONyY0iRS.problem: Although entropy is invariant to factorization order, a finite learner may acquire some prediction orders more efficiently than others.
x9ONyY0iRS.method: The authors quantify order-learnability via prequential codelength, accumulating log-loss as a Transformer predicts each batch before training on it. They calibrate the metric synthetically and evaluate 21 fixed orders across 12 corpora.
x9ONyY0iRS.key_idea: Accumulates prequential log-loss before each training batch under a controlled Transformer protocol to compare learning efficiency across factorization orders.
x9ONyY0iRS.evidence: Controlled Transformer experiments across 21 fixed orders and 12 corpora, including text, mathematical chain-of-thought traces, protein sources, and English Wikipedia.
x9ONyY0iRS.claimed_gains: Left-to-right is uniquely best only on mathematical chain-of-thought traces; reversal accounts for at most 5.5% of global-shuffle excess on text versus 50–62% for four-token local shuffling (from review).
x9ONyY0iRS.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the paper investigates a meaningful, well-motivated question using broad empirical experimentation and a sensible prequential codelength measure.
x9ONyY0iRS.main_concern: The results rely on a single Transformer learner with order-specific learning rate tuning and offer limited mechanistic explanation for the observed differences.

MkFAa2ZOmA.one_liner: Demonstrates multi-hop prompt-injection propagation across independent stateful AI assistants via shared user-exchanged artifacts.
MkFAa2ZOmA.problem: Stateful assistants that store content from shared documents into persistent memory create an indirect cross-user channel for self-propagating attacks.
MkFAa2ZOmA.method: The authors model artifact-mediated propagation in temporal human-agent universes where an infected document enters assistant memory, gets reproduced in newly created artifacts, and spreads to other users' assistants.
MkFAa2ZOmA.key_idea: Uses shared user artifacts to hop adversarial instructions across isolated assistants' persistent memories and newly generated documents.
MkFAa2ZOmA.evidence: Simulations in temporal human-agent universes across four models under endpoint-assisted and prompt-only variants.
MkFAa2ZOmA.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the artifact-mediated cross-assistant attack surface is practically relevant and highlights a realistic vulnerability in stateful agent workflows.
MkFAa2ZOmA.main_concern: Headline propagation results rely on an attacker-controlled endpoint server restoring the full payload rather than autonomous prompt-only self-replication.

SrBlVXzuG2.one_liner: Investigates when retaining failed agent context helps or hurts recovery across information availability, failed code, and checkpointing.
SrBlVXzuG2.problem: After an agent fails, retaining its previous context mixes useful observations with misleading errors, making it unclear when recovery benefits over starting fresh.
SrBlVXzuG2.method: The authors conduct controlled interventions varying correct facts inside and outside retained records, exposure to failed code, training failure sources, and conversation retention at restored file checkpoints. They evaluate recovery against both shared-context and fresh-generation baselines.
SrBlVXzuG2.key_idea: Isolates retained-context effects by holding misleading errors fixed while varying correct facts inside versus outside the record and comparing against fresh-start baselines.
SrBlVXzuG2.evidence: Experiments span 80 ScrambleToolBench states, 60 ALFWorld states, and 34 repository failures across Qwen3-8B, Llama-3.1-8B, and Gemma-4-12B-it.
SrBlVXzuG2.claimed_gains: Retaining an old tool map shifts benefit from +7.7 to -6.6 percentage points for Qwen3-8B and +1.9 to -8.3 for Llama-3.1-8B depending on external mappings, while showing failed code reduces task-only success by 16.0 points.
SrBlVXzuG2.reviewer_consensus: Two reviewers praise the careful dose-grid and checkpoint interventions that isolate where information resides and show the importance of fresh-start baselines.
SrBlVXzuG2.main_concern: Reviewers note that the four experiments are loosely connected without a unifying rule, offer incremental extensions over prior work, and face complaints of poor organization and incomplete ALFWorld results.

iCXoGTzekp.one_liner: Adapts time-series forecasters at test time without gradient updates by retrieving historical episodes from an online memory bank.
iCXoGTzekp.problem: Parameter-update test-time adaptation in time-series forecasting can overwrite model weights from local feedback and harm predictions in unrelated contexts.
iCXoGTzekp.method: OREM (Online Retrieval Episodic Memory) accumulates deployment episodes in an online memory bank and retrieves relevant historical episodes at inference to compute calibrated residual corrections without updating backbone parameters.
iCXoGTzekp.key_idea: Replaces continual parameter updates in time-series TTA with retrieval-based residual correction from a causally accumulated online episodic memory bank.
iCXoGTzekp.evidence: Experiments across five forecasting backbones, six datasets, and four forecast horizons, plus component ablations.
iCXoGTzekp.claimed_gains: OREM reduces MSE and MAE by 5.43% (exact second figure truncated in abstract).
iCXoGTzekp.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the parameter-free episodic retrieval approach simple, practical, and broadly evaluated across backbones, datasets, and horizons.
iCXoGTzekp.main_concern: Reviewers point out missing comparisons against retrieval-based forecasting baselines (e.g., RAFT, PFRP, SOLID, OneNet) and lack of multi-seed variance or statistical tests.

l8jqfdwJdN.one_liner: Exposes inter-agent communication protocols as textual optimization variables co-evolved with agent prompts from feedback.
l8jqfdwJdN.problem: Multi-agent optimization frameworks tune agent prompts or workflows while leaving inter-agent communication protocols fixed.
l8jqfdwJdN.method: EvoProtocol parameterizes the inter-agent communication protocol as an explicit textual object and jointly optimizes it with agent prompts using execution feedback and segment-level handoff signals.
l8jqfdwJdN.key_idea: Treats inter-agent communication protocols as optimizable textual variables co-evolved alongside agent prompts.
l8jqfdwJdN.evidence: Evaluations on five MAS-PromptBench tasks and BrowseComp-Plus with a dynamic planner-executor workflow.
l8jqfdwJdN.claimed_gains: On BrowseComp-Plus, EvoProtocol improves accuracy by 5.5–16 points over prompt optimization with default and PACT protocols, while its cost-aware variant matches PACT accuracy at about 24% lower cost.
l8jqfdwJdN.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that making inter-agent communication protocols an explicit optimization variable is a timely, practical extension to prompt optimization.
l8jqfdwJdN.main_concern: Reviewers point out unfair comparisons where EvoProtocol receives extra diagnostics and tokens not given to prompt-only baselines, and lacks comparisons against MAS-specific optimizers like MIPROv2 or MAPRO.

1d2LzezE1I.one_liner: Replaces independent marginal cost-risk constraints in constrained RL with a single joint CVaR constraint along the Lagrange-multiplier path.
1d2LzezE1I.problem: Independent marginal cost-risk constraints in constrained RL penalize unrealizable joint events and produce overly conservative policies.
1d2LzezE1I.method: JRCPO preserves expected-cost constraints while unifying marginal risk constraints into a single CVaR constraint over a scalarized reward-cost objective evaluated along the Lagrange multiplier direction using a Gaussian joint critic.
1d2LzezE1I.key_idea: Evaluate a single Gaussian-approximated CVaR constraint on the Lagrange-scalarized reward-cost return to capture cost-reward correlations and avoid unrealizable worst-case combinations.
1d2LzezE1I.evidence: Experiments on multi-cost RL tasks compare JRCPO against expected-cost and marginal-risk-sensitive baselines.
1d2LzezE1I.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that avoiding overly conservative marginal risk constraints on negatively correlated costs is a well-motivated problem.
1d2LzezE1I.main_concern: Reviewers criticize the strong Gaussian joint-return assumption and question whether the dual CVaR formulation actually differs from componentwise risk constraints.

IYLR6MlZMV.one_liner: Analyzes attention and selective state-space models via second-order complexity bounds accounting for accuracy, regularity, and precision locality.
IYLR6MlZMV.problem: Sequence-length complexity alone does not determine the resources needed to evaluate sequence models at a prescribed approximation accuracy.
IYLR6MlZMV.method: The authors formulate a second-order complexity analysis for representative attention and selective state-space operators, deriving deterministic sampling bounds and introducing precision locality as the shortest recent context needed to recover full-history outputs.
IYLR6MlZMV.key_idea: Separates signal-resolution sampling cost from required history length via deterministic smoothness bounds and precision locality under contractive selective scans.
IYLR6MlZMV.evidence: Theoretical analysis establishing matching upper and lower sampling bounds on continuous Lipschitz, smooth, and analytic input classes and discrete bounded token sequences.
IYLR6MlZMV.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that decomposing evaluation cost into sample density and history length yields clean, rigorous theoretical bounds separating attention from state-space models.
IYLR6MlZMV.main_concern: The results rely on strong continuous smoothness assumptions and simplified attention setups, with no empirical validation on trained models or discrete language tasks.

m8e25icYJN.one_liner: Designs a negative-binomial-difference count reference process jointly defining Schrödinger bridge couplings and tractable integer-valued bridges for perturbation prediction.
m8e25icYJN.problem: Unpaired single-cell perturbation prediction via optimal transport suffers when heterogeneous response amplitudes distort correspondences and when coupling costs mismatch the bridge reference process.
m8e25icYJN.method: PerturbBridge introduces a two-parameter negative-binomial-difference count reference family that separates displacement scale from tail shape at fixed variance. Each reference induces both a Schrödinger endpoint coupling and a matching tractable integer-valued conditional bridge for generation.
m8e25icYJN.key_idea: Uses a two-parameter negative-binomial-difference reference process to jointly define endpoint Schrödinger couplings and matching integer-valued bridges while controlling tail shape independently of variance.
m8e25icYJN.evidence: Supported by two-state correspondence-preservation theory and empirical evaluation on unseen cell-type perturbation transfer (including PBMC subsets) and 1,080-group sensitivity ablations.
m8e25icYJN.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the unified reference-process design—connecting endpoint coupling and bridge dynamics with decoupled scale and shape—mathematically coherent and well-motivated.
m8e25icYJN.main_concern: Reviewers note that multistep bridge generation is not isolated from direct conditional generation on the same couplings, and full-benchmark comparisons against the Poisson reference and recent baselines are incomplete.

HvJvbRZ14D.one_liner: Synthesizes coherent terminal agent tasks, executable environments, and expert trajectories jointly from agent skill specifications.
HvJvbRZ14D.problem: Existing terminal agent data pipelines synthesize instructions, environments, and trajectories in isolation, causing coherence failures as data scales.
HvJvbRZ14D.method: Terminal-World uses agent skills—encoding goals, applicability, and execution—as a unified primitive to jointly derive tasks, Docker/executable environments, automatic verifiers, and guided trajectories, creating the Terminal-Atlas dataset (5.7K trajectories) to train Terminal-Navigator-8B/14B/32B.
HvJvbRZ14D.key_idea: Jointly derives task instructions, executable environments, verifiers, and expert trajectories from a single agent-skill specification rather than synthesizing components independently.
HvJvbRZ14D.evidence: Evaluated on Terminal-Bench 2.0 and six benchmarks across 8B, 14B, and 32B Terminal-Navigator models with SFT and GRPO.
HvJvbRZ14D.claimed_gains: Using 1.2% of the training data, Terminal-Navigator-32B achieves 31.5 vs. 27.0 Pass@1 and 43.8 vs. 37.1 Pass@3 on Terminal-Bench 2.0 compared to the same teacher/base baseline.
HvJvbRZ14D.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers highlight the strong sample efficiency on Terminal-Bench 2.0 using only ~5.7K trajectories compared to 490.5K in Nemotron-Terminal.
HvJvbRZ14D.main_concern: Reviewers note the lack of controlled experiments isolating unified skill-based synthesis from isolated pipelines under matched budgets, plus potential false positives in generated verifier code.

3KFpcMYaws.one_liner: Retains the previous rollout batch alongside newly collected samples in large-scale parallel PPO to stabilize policy updates.
3KFpcMYaws.problem: Large-scale parallel PPO suffers from learning instability and collapse on complex, long-horizon tasks with high-dimensional action spaces.
3KFpcMYaws.method: RAgger modifies PPO by retaining the immediately preceding rollout batch and optimizing jointly over old and new samples to regularize the policy trajectory against local forgetting.
3KFpcMYaws.key_idea: Aggregates the previous rollout batch with the current batch in PPO to regularize policy optimization against local forgetting.
3KFpcMYaws.evidence: Evaluations and ablations on challenging dexterous manipulation tasks (AllegroKuka) compared against PPO, SAPG, and CPO.
3KFpcMYaws.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers praise the simplicity of the modification, the strong manipulation results over SAPG/CPO, and the well-designed ablations.
3KFpcMYaws.main_concern: The method closely overlaps with existing rollout-reuse algorithms like AMBER and off-policy PPO, and experiments do not causally prove local forgetting drives PPO collapse.

O0n61rKe9T.one_liner: Learns set-conditioned marginal frame gain and stopping decisions via supervised initialization and RL for long video QA.
O0n61rKe9T.problem: Long-form video QA frame selectors rely on predefined search or trajectory-level outcomes without modeling a candidate frame's marginal information gain over already selected frames.
O0n61rKe9T.method: SetGain conditions a lightweight gain model on the candidate pool and current selected set to predict each remaining frame's marginal value and when to stop, trained via supervised marginal temporal-coverage initialization followed by RL with answer-quality and coverage rewards.
O0n61rKe9T.key_idea: Predicts each candidate frame's marginal gain conditioned on the evolving selected set to jointly choose the next frame and stopping point.
O0n61rKe9T.evidence: Evaluated on Haystack-LVBench, VideoMME, MLVU, and LongVideoBench against pointwise top-k, TimeSearch-R, T*, TSPO, AKS, and Q-Frame.
O0n61rKe9T.claimed_gains: Improves temporal F1 by 11.3% relative over pointwise top-k with 22% fewer frames on Haystack-LVBench, reaches 2.31x TimeSearch-R temporal F1 and 5.3-7.0 points higher QA accuracy, and improves average QA accuracy by 3.4 points over top-k and 5.2 points (8.3% relative) over prior work with 53.7% lower latency (2.16x speedup) than T*.
O0n61rKe9T.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers acknowledge the controlled Haystack-LVBench comparisons and the lightweight, fast 2.17M-parameter selector design.
O0n61rKe9T.main_concern: Reviewers note that large end-to-end QA gains mainly stem from the event pool and reranker rather than set conditioning, and matched top-k controls are missing on other benchmarks.

nAfSQdjWb4.one_liner: Shows that LLM server co-batching alters agent tool executions, database states, and task success even from identical requests.
nAfSQdjWb4.problem: Serving batching introduces text nondeterminism, but its downstream impact on stateful tool-using agent trajectories and task outcomes is unmeasured.
nAfSQdjWb4.method: The authors hold target requests fixed in AppWorld while varying co-batch conditions, executing actions from checkpoints, restoring common database states to isolate supplied-history effects, and testing deterministic serving configurations.
nAfSQdjWb4.key_idea: Measures executable tool forks, database-state divergence, and history-induced trajectory splits under controlled inference co-batching.
nAfSQdjWb4.evidence: Evaluated in AppWorld across five deployment panels, 97 selected fork states, 16 new tasks, and controlled Qwen, DeepSeek, and MiniMax audits.
nAfSQdjWb4.claimed_gains: Repeatable operational forks occur in 4 of 5 panels, and paired continuations differ on task checks in 36 of 97 evaluable selected states within an eight-decision window.
nAfSQdjWb4.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the execution-grounded methodology that traces serving nondeterminism through tool calls, database states, and task checks.
nAfSQdjWb4.main_concern: Findings on unselected tasks are inconclusive, co-batch occupancy is confounded with companion request composition, and the low-level numerical root causes remain unidentified.

B6oc904vwC.one_liner: Verifies nearest-neighbor candidates progressively in an orthogonal basis and prunes early using a Cauchy-Schwarz distance lower bound.
B6oc904vwC.problem: High-dimensional distance verification of candidate vectors dominates query time in approximate nearest-neighbor search even though most candidates fail top-k.
B6oc904vwC.method: Panorama rotates vectors into a data-fitted orthogonal basis, accumulates partial distances piecewise, and prunes candidates once a Cauchy-Schwarz lower bound on unread coordinates exceeds the running top-k threshold, integrating into IVF, PQ, graph, reranking, and RaBitQ indexes.
B6oc904vwC.key_idea: Rotates embeddings into a variance-concentrated orthogonal basis and applies progressive Cauchy-Schwarz lower bounds to abort candidate distance checks early.
B6oc904vwC.evidence: Integrated into five index families and evaluated across multiple vector-search datasets (including SIFT, GIST, and Large).
B6oc904vwC.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper targets a real ANNS bottleneck with a sound deterministic pruning bound and multi-index implementations.
B6oc904vwC.main_concern: Compressed-index score accounting and equal-budget comparisons need clarification, basis-transform costs and parameter selection are underspecified, and undefined jargon hinders readability.

F7hMQVx5TX.one_liner: Proves manifold curvature blocks differentiable classifiers from being simultaneously accurate and off-manifold invariant, proposing path-integral evaluation.
F7hMQVx5TX.problem: Why differentiable classifiers struggle to achieve both high accuracy and adversarial robustness on curved data manifolds.
F7hMQVx5TX.method: The paper decomposes the tangent-projected gradient field of a classifier to show its antisymmetric curl scales with manifold curvature, obstructing conservative differentiable representations, and tests relaxing conservativeness via path-dependent line-integral classifiers.
F7hMQVx5TX.key_idea: Shows manifold curvature induces non-zero curl in tangent-projected sensitivity fields, preventing conservative differentiable functions from being both accurate and strongly tangent.
F7hMQVx5TX.evidence: Supported by differential-geometric proofs (including a rigidity theorem on S^1) and empirical tests on MNIST and FashionMNIST.
F7hMQVx5TX.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the vector-field calculus perspective on the robustness-accuracy trade-off novel and theoretically interesting.
F7hMQVx5TX.main_concern: Path-integral classifiers are computationally impractical for larger datasets, experiments are limited to small datasets with simple tangent approximations, and related theoretical literature is missing.

Xv6vvkGx4N.one_liner: Forecasting agency-registered fires on a complete national hex grid supplies an open rare-event benchmark beyond satellite detections.
Xv6vvkGx4N.problem: Wildfire benchmarks rely on satellite observations that miss many smaller agency-registered fires, especially where detection varies with fire size.
Xv6vvkGx4N.method: The benchmark covers 83 Russian regions with daily cell labels, openly licensed weather inputs, temporal splits, and complete-grid evaluation under extreme imbalance. A gradient-boosted baseline is compared with climatology and fire-danger indices at a fixed alarm budget.
Xv6vvkGx4N.key_idea: Registered-fire labels and fixed-budget alarm metrics measure operationally relevant rare-event prediction over every national grid cell rather than sampled negatives.
Xv6vvkGx4N.evidence: The dataset spans 64,620 cells, April-October seasons from 2000 to 2024, 420,995 registered fires, and evaluation across 807 days of four fire seasons.
Xv6vvkGx4N.claimed_gains: At a 15.2% grid alarm budget, the baseline catches 80.5% of daily fire cells versus 63.7% for climatology, 53.6% for the Canadian Fire Weather Index, and 47.9% for the Russian statutory index.
Xv6vvkGx4N.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that administrative records, national coverage, natural imbalance, and redistributable inputs make the benchmark useful for rare-event prediction.
Xv6vvkGx4N.main_concern: Reviewers most often question the forecasting claim because same-day weather and possible later data inputs do not establish advance-warning performance.

PJVGe9MqTS.one_liner: Generating reference-relative trajectory deformations and prioritizing collision safety lets a selector refine frozen driving planners post hoc.
PJVGe9MqTS.problem: End-to-end planners can emit colliding trajectories even when a small adjustment would avoid the collision, and retraining changes their acquired behavior.
PJVGe9MqTS.method: SRTDrive keeps the frozen planner's trajectory as a reference and generates alternatives through path-relative deformations. A selector scores candidates against the reference using supervision that rejects collision-increasing replacements before considering trajectory error.
PJVGe9MqTS.key_idea: Reference-relative candidate scoring uses lexicographic supervision so collision safety determines replacement eligibility and trajectory error only ranks equally safe options.
PJVGe9MqTS.evidence: Evaluation includes closed-loop Bench2Drive tests with VAD-Base and application to seven frozen planners on nuScenes without retraining.
PJVGe9MqTS.claimed_gains: On Bench2Drive, SRTDrive raises VAD-Base Driving Score from 43.07 to 47.77 and reduces collision routes from 95 to 86; on nuScenes, it lowers L2 error for five planners and collision rate for three.
PJVGe9MqTS.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that retaining the original plan among generated alternatives provides a practical way to refine frozen planners without changing their weights.
PJVGe9MqTS.main_concern: Reviewers most often find comparative evidence insufficient to isolate the selector's benefit or establish general safety gains across planners.

hVEdVHa3du.one_liner: Characterizes when local MARL credit assignment inflates shared policy-gradient variance and introduces PLACID to admit and realize variance-reducing corrections.
hVEdVHa3du.problem: Under parameter sharing in MARL, reducing each individual agent's gradient variance can change inter-agent gradient correlations and worsen the variance of the summed shared gradient.
hVEdVHa3du.method: The authors construct counterexamples where locally optimal critics arbitrarily inflate shared-gradient variance, derive exact covariance criteria, and propose PLACID, which decides whether and how strongly to admit a zero-mean correction on the shared gradient before reducing its sampling noise.
hVEdVHa3du.key_idea: Tests and scales zero-mean local credit-assignment corrections after shared-gradient aggregation (admission) and reduces correction sampling noise (realization).
hVEdVHa3du.evidence: Theoretical counterexamples and covariance criteria plus experiments on 16 tabular games, two fitted-critic families, and SMAC/MA-MuJoCo diagnostics.
hVEdVHa3du.claimed_gains: On 16 fixed tabular games, empirical admission removes up to 9.21% of sparse population mean-squared error.
hVEdVHa3du.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the counterintuitive theoretical insight on shared-gradient covariance under parameter sharing and the principled Bernstein-bound admission mechanism.
hVEdVHa3du.main_concern: End-to-end learning gains on standard MARL benchmarks (SMAC, MA-MuJoCo) remain inconclusive, the certified variant often abstains on small batches, and heavy bespoke terminology hampers readability.

EcMbDqixxy.one_liner: Characterizes Conflict of Skills attacks where locally admitted LLM agent skills compose into policy violations, and introduces CoSA-Bench.
EcMbDqixxy.problem: Security checks that vet individual LLM agent skills in isolation miss policy violations arising when benign skills are composed downstream.
EcMbDqixxy.method: The authors identify four Conflict of Skills mechanisms, introduce the Conflict of Skills Attack (CoSA) adding locally admitted skills for capability supplementation or relationship reshaping without changing permissions, and build CoSA-Bench (288 tasks across four domains).
EcMbDqixxy.key_idea: Adds statically admitted skills that supply missing business operations or reshape cross-skill artifact/decision bindings to trigger compositional policy violations.
EcMbDqixxy.evidence: Evaluated on CoSA-Bench (288 tasks across recruiting, finance, IT, and business) spanning five LLMs and three agent harnesses.
EcMbDqixxy.claimed_gains: Skill additions capped at 5% of each original pool raise policy-violation rates from 35.02% to 58.45% (+23.43 percentage points).
EcMbDqixxy.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that composition-level security risks across individually vetted agent skills represent a timely and underexplored attack surface, well-tested across models and harnesses.
EcMbDqixxy.main_concern: The threat model assumes attacker visibility into the victim's skill pool, and static-scanner admission does not establish that added skills are individually harmless at runtime.

BwO4dhJyji.one_liner: Evaluates VLM modality control via counterfactual Flip/Stay metrics and learns single-token modality neologisms with Counterfactual Twin-Margin supervision.
BwO4dhJyji.problem: Standard accuracy cannot tell whether a VLM genuinely follows a user-requested modality (image vs. caption) under conflict or relies on pretrained priors.
BwO4dhJyji.method: The authors introduce counterfactual Flip and Stay metrics under image/caption edits and train single-token neologism embeddings in a frozen VLM using Counterfactual Twin-Margin (CTM) supervision on paired interventions.
BwO4dhJyji.key_idea: Trains one new vocabulary embedding per modality on a frozen VLM using paired counterfactual twin-margin supervision to enforce modality-specific Flip and Stay behavior.
BwO4dhJyji.evidence: Evaluated across three VLMs and four benchmarks (including Ground-CF and MultiVENT-G) against natural-language instructions, fixed-prefix prompt tuning, and LoRA.
BwO4dhJyji.claimed_gains: Single-embedding neologisms retain strong visual and textual control on held-out values while LoRA uses 5,300–11,600x more trainable parameters.
BwO4dhJyji.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers strongly approve of the counterfactual Flip/Stay evaluation design that separates genuine modality following from static accuracy.
BwO4dhJyji.main_concern: The advantage of neologisms over matched prompt tuning or simple training-free input filtering is not fully established, and held-out generalization and token interpretability remain limited.

4IVaoJcgX0.one_liner: Defines local sensitivity for decision tree ensembles, proves parameterized hardness, reduces explainability and monitoring to it, and solves via RegEnum/MILP.
4IVaoJcgX0.problem: Existing sensitivity analyses for decision tree ensembles focus on global feature agreement rather than local feature-subset perturbations around a specific input.
4IVaoJcgX0.method: The authors formalize local sensitivity for decision tree ensembles, prove NP-completeness and W[1]-hardness (with a depth-1 vs. depth-2 complexity split), reduce contrastive explainability and runtime monitoring to local sensitivity, and solve it via region enumeration (RegEnum) and MILP.
4IVaoJcgX0.key_idea: Unifies local robustness, contrastive explanations, and monitoring of tree ensembles under local feature-subset sensitivity solved by region enumeration or MILP.
4IVaoJcgX0.evidence: Parameterized complexity proofs, reductions, and prototype runtime benchmarks comparing RegEnum and MILP against dedicated tools like XReason.
4IVaoJcgX0.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the unified theoretical formulation of local sensitivity and its parameterized complexity results (including W[1]-hardness and depth split).
4IVaoJcgX0.main_concern: Core algorithms (RegEnum and MILP) closely adapt prior work, RegEnum scales poorly beyond very small feature subsets, and the subset-minimal explanation loop has a potential correctness flaw.

cUQAUr8bnT.one_liner: Table-Zero self-improves multi-table reasoning by constructing joinable/decomposable table tasks with SQL-verified answers and iteratively training proposer and solver.
cUQAUr8bnT.problem: Self-improving RL for multi-table reasoning struggles because models fail to synthesize multi-table questions with reliable reference answers without human labels.
cUQAUr8bnT.method: Table-Zero exploits table joinability and lossless decomposition to select related tables, prompts a proposer to generate questions and reference SQL executed for exact answers, and iteratively trains the proposer with DPO and the solver with RL over three rounds.
cUQAUr8bnT.key_idea: Uses table joinability and lossless decomposition to synthesize multi-table questions whose reference answers come from executing proposer-generated SQL, alternating DPO proposer and RL solver updates.
cUQAUr8bnT.evidence: Evaluated across seven table-reasoning datasets using Qwen3-8B and Qwen3-14B over three self-improvement iterations against prompting and adapted self-improvement baselines.
cUQAUr8bnT.claimed_gains: Across seven datasets, achieves 32.3% average exact match with Qwen3-8B and 37.0% with Qwen3-14B, compared with 20.4% and 24.3% for prompting.
cUQAUr8bnT.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers like the practical use of table joinability, lossless decomposition, and SQL execution to produce verifiable multi-table training tasks without human labels.
