cUQAUr8bnT.main_concern: Solver optimization differences (online group filtering, difficulty weighting, rollout budgets, and checkpoint selection) confound comparisons with Dr.Zero and SPICE, preventing clean attribution to task construction.

4xaVia45va.one_liner: Combines bounded Haar multipliers and symbol-generated paraproducts on binary trees for linear-work multiscale neural operators.
4xaVia45va.problem: Capturing cross-scale physical-field interactions can cause coupling coefficients to accumulate uncontrollably with hierarchy depth even when individually bounded.
4xaVia45va.method: Haar Paraproduct Neural Operator (HPNO) pairs a bounded Haar multiplier with mean-to-detail and detail-to-mean transfers driven by two bounded input-conditioned symbols across a weighted binary hierarchy. Shared upward and downward tree passes evaluate the full kernel action in linear work without forming a dense kernel matrix.
4xaVia45va.key_idea: Derives directional multiscale couplings from two bounded symbols over orthogonal binary-tree regions to enforce a depth-independent weighted L2 bound.
4xaVia45va.evidence: Evaluated on six PDE benchmarks spanning grids, meshes, and point clouds plus two unstructured CFD benchmarks, alongside theoretical weighted L2 bounds, reciprocal kernel replacements, multi-resolution scaling, and ablations.
4xaVia45va.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers praise the mathematically grounded formulation with depth-independent weighted L2 bounds, linear-cost geometry-agnostic tree passes, and strong benchmark results.
4xaVia45va.main_concern: Improvements cannot be clearly attributed to the paraproduct kernel because HPNO adds task-specific extras like local convolutions, gradient losses, and refinement modules that baselines lack.

0JZ2YTpSbh.one_liner: Trains cooperative MARL policies with a pluggable adversarial topology mask generator to resist execution-time link failures.
0JZ2YTpSbh.problem: Cooperative multi-agent reinforcement learning methods rely on inter-agent communication and degrade when communication links disconnect at execution.
0JZ2YTpSbh.method: PatMask introduces a pluggable adversarial mask generator that adaptively disrupts critical communication links during training via an alternating adversarial training procedure. It pairs this training scheme with a proven contraction property for robust policy evaluation under topology perturbations.
0JZ2YTpSbh.key_idea: Alternately trains an adversarial mask generator to drop critical communication edges during MARL training without adding execution-time modules.
0JZ2YTpSbh.evidence: Evaluated across cooperative MARL benchmarks with GAT, GCN, and TGCNET backbones under controlled disconnection types and probabilities, supported by a contraction proof.
0JZ2YTpSbh.claimed_gains: Achieves win rates 15.7-41.6 percentage points higher than unaugmented baselines using 41% of the training steps.
0JZ2YTpSbh.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers highlight PatMask's simplicity, plug-and-play integration into existing topology-aware MARL architectures without execution overhead, and strong empirical performance across disconnection settings.
0JZ2YTpSbh.main_concern: Gains over random dropout baselines are modest and confounded by mismatched link-removal rates, while mask equations and gradient paths need clearer specification.

KJwkXJ9y93.one_liner: Establishes minimax rates for four-meaning semantic entropy from weak pairwise judgments using edge, wedge, and three-star averages.
KJwkXJ9y93.problem: Under a weak noisy pairwise equivalence judge, edge and wedge averages determine semantic entropy for at most three meanings but fail to identify four meanings.
KJwkXJ9y93.method: The authors model the judge as a known homogeneous channel on the complete verdict graph and add the three-star average to recover the missing fourth collision moment. They propose an estimator that projects the three subgraph averages onto the valid moment set and solves a quartic, alongside matching minimax lower bounds.
KJwkXJ9y93.key_idea: Augments edge and wedge verdict-graph averages with three-star averages, projecting moments onto the valid set and solving a quartic.
KJwkXJ9y93.evidence: Theoretical minimax upper and lower bounds on polynomial windows for n answers with at most four meanings, accompanied by synthetic simulations and query-design results.
KJwkXJ9y93.claimed_gains: Establishes minimax squared risk of order min{1, (n^4 Delta^6)^(-1/3)} with critical exponent 2/3 for four meanings versus 3/4 for three meanings.
KJwkXJ9y93.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the sharp minimax characterization, the identification of three-star statistics for four meanings, and the rigorous matching lower-bound proof.
KJwkXJ9y93.main_concern: The analysis relies on restrictive homogeneous independent judge assumptions and synthetic experiments only, with no evaluation on real LLM outputs or judges.

pxsefnckQy.one_liner: Uses multi-scale functional-unit constraints and inferred residue roles to guide modality-adaptive flow matching for antibody co-design.
pxsefnckQy.problem: Existing antibody co-design models treat sequence and structure modalities uniformly, ignoring scale-dependent biophysical constraints and context-dependent residue roles.
pxsefnckQy.method: MoDA decomposes functional-unit representations to model local-to-global constraints and infers cooperation-aware residue roles from residue constraints and inter-residue coordination. It then uses these constraints and roles to direct message passing and asymmetric cross-modal updates within a flow-matching framework.
pxsefnckQy.key_idea: Infers context-dependent residue roles from multi-scale functional-unit constraints to drive role-directed message passing and asymmetric cross-modal flow-matching updates.
pxsefnckQy.evidence: Evaluated on the RAbD antibody co-design benchmark measuring structural fidelity and computational binding-energy success rate.
pxsefnckQy.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers note clear biological motivation, coherent integration of multi-scale and modality-specific modules, and strong structural accuracy on RAbD (reducing CDR RMSD from 1.8139 to 1.5780).
pxsefnckQy.main_concern: Reported metrics are inconsistent across tables (for example, G-lDDT of 0.8341 versus 0.7668) and several mathematical definitions, candidate aggregations, and component justifications lack clarity.

O4jRp4NwhQ.one_liner: Synthesizes chunk-aligned backward recovery trajectories for training and filters candidate chunks by cycle-consistency at inference.
O4jRp4NwhQ.problem: Generative action-chunking policies suffer from covariate shift, while existing corrective augmentations generate isolated transitions that break temporal chunk coherence.
O4jRp4NwhQ.method: ReSynC uses a truncated backward diffusion policy and backward dynamics model to synthesize a plausible deviation and recovery, replacing the prefix of an expert action chunk. At inference, it reuses the dynamics models to score candidate chunks by cycle-consistency error and contrastively selects low-error candidates.
O4jRp4NwhQ.key_idea: Replaces expert action-chunk prefixes with backward-diffused deviation-and-recovery segments during training and selects inference chunks by bidirectional dynamics cycle consistency.
O4jRp4NwhQ.evidence: Evaluated across five simulation tasks (including Transport, Kitchen, and Push-T) with Diffusion Policy and a factorial study of backward generators and stitching strategies.
O4jRp4NwhQ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the well-motivated chunk-aligned formulation, the factorial analysis isolating backward generator and stitching interactions, and consistent gains over Diffusion Policy across simulation tasks.
O4jRp4NwhQ.main_concern: Synthesized recovery trajectories are only validated indirectly via task success rather than checking whether executing them actually returns the robot to expert states under true dynamics.

c1cOAhi3DD.one_liner: Aggregates step-size-tied clipped OGD experts with bias offsets for comparator-uniform heavy-tailed dynamic regret.
c1cOAhi3DD.problem: High-probability dynamic regret bounds under heavy-tailed gradients previously required pre-fixed comparators, horizon knowledge, or extra logarithmic horizon factors.
c1cOAhi3DD.method: The algorithm aggregates clipped online-gradient-descent experts over a learning-rate grid anchored at the static statistical scale, tying each expert's clipping threshold to its step size with a per-expert bias offset. An analysis-only auxiliary descent sequence converts comparator-dependent noise residuals into a predictable martingale without extra samples.
c1cOAhi3DD.key_idea: Pairs bias-offset aggregation of threshold-tied clipped OGD experts with an analysis-only auxiliary descent sequence to yield single-event comparator-uniform bounds.
c1cOAhi3DD.evidence: Theoretical high-probability regret proofs on bounded convex sets with adaptively chosen convex Lipschitz losses and bounded conditional p-th central moment noise for p in (1, 2].
c1cOAhi3DD.claimed_gains: Obtains a single probability-(1-delta) dynamic regret bound valid over all prefixes and comparator paths scaling with sqrt(T) and T^(1/p) terms.
c1cOAhi3DD.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize the technical soundness of relaxing fixed-comparator assumptions to hindsight paths via the auxiliary descent analysis.
c1cOAhi3DD.main_concern: The paper has limited experimental comparisons, requires prior knowledge of problem scale parameters (D, G, sigma, p), and has unclear presentation and positioning against prior work.

i7FAbxlwgd.one_liner: Dynamically builds paper-specific review rubrics from distilled historical review checks and related-paper reviews, then retrieves paper evidence per item.
i7FAbxlwgd.problem: Most AI peer reviewers apply a single fixed rubric across all papers and are benchmarked mainly on aggregate ICLR averages that hide cross-domain differences.
i7FAbxlwgd.method: DynReviewer is a training-free agent that reads a submission, adapts general checks distilled from past human reviews alongside reviews of related papers into a paper-specific rubric, and searches the paper for grounded evidence on each check. The authors also build ReviewAtlas-40K+ (45,551 papers from six venues) and ReviewAtlas-Bench (2025 papers across four venues and four ICLR domains).
i7FAbxlwgd.key_idea: Rewrites distilled historical review checks and retrieved related-paper reviews into a paper-specific rubric and searches the manuscript for grounded evidence without model training.
i7FAbxlwgd.evidence: Evaluated across three LLM backbones on ReviewAtlas-Bench (four venues and four ICLR domains) with component ablations and source-exclusion analyses.
i7FAbxlwgd.claimed_gains: Leads the strongest same-backbone baseline by 5.6 to 19.9 percentage points at covering human reviewers' concerns with paper-grounded criticisms.
i7FAbxlwgd.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the training-free rubric-adaptation design is practical and delivers consistent empirical improvements across three LLM backbones and multiple venues.
i7FAbxlwgd.main_concern: Reviewers note limited novelty over prior adaptive/memory-based AI reviewers (e.g., TreeReview, ScholarPeer), weak evidence for domain-specific vs paper-specific adaptation, and uncalibrated LLM-judge evaluation against noisy human reviews.

wRtLmU14Kp.one_liner: Derives unbiased inverse-weighted estimators and finite-batch allocation criteria for randomized verification budgets in RL without treating timeouts as failures.
wRtLmU14Kp.problem: Treating verification timeouts as negative rewards in RLVR biases the policy gradient against slower correct programs, altering the optimization objective.
wRtLmU14Kp.method: Building on inverse probability weighting and randomized truncation, the authors derive a finite-minibatch verification-allocation criterion from a smooth improvement bound that includes a squared-mean-gradient term. They characterize the minimum number of independent censored records (two for the usual product, three for the finite-batch criterion) needed for universally unbiased allocation feedback and construct distinct-record estimators.
wRtLmU14Kp.key_idea: Uses randomized verification truncation with inverse-probability weighting and distinct-record censored estimators to preserve unbiased policy gradients while optimizing finite-batch verification budgets.
wRtLmU14Kp.evidence: Supported by theoretical derivations, a high-signal control study, and an executed-program study with a 48-parameter linear softmax policy.
wRtLmU14Kp.claimed_gains: In a high-signal control, shifting verification probability from 1 to ~0.112 reduces the finite-batch objective by 47.6%.
wRtLmU14Kp.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that distinguishing verification timeouts from task failures is a genuine issue and that the finite-batch allocation theory and unbiased estimators are mathematically rigorous.
wRtLmU14Kp.main_concern: Reviewers note that empirical evaluation is restricted to small synthetic/toy setups where the learned allocation does not beat a simpler fixed schedule or full verification under matched CPU time.

sAYkoo4ufN.one_liner: Assigns step-level RL credit via action-family rubrics mean-centered within matched state groups for long-horizon agents.
sAYkoo4ufN.problem: Outcome-derived process signals in long-horizon agentic reinforcement learning entangle local action quality with downstream consequences.
sAYkoo4ufN.method: ACRE evaluates intermediate actions using reusable rubrics defined per functional action family to produce semantic process rewards. These rewards are mean-centered within matched environment-state groups to form relative process advantages combined with episode-level outcome advantages.
sAYkoo4ufN.key_idea: Evaluates intermediate actions with reusable action-family rubrics and mean-centers the resulting process rewards within matched pre-decision state groups for policy optimization.
sAYkoo4ufN.evidence: Evaluated on ALFWorld and WebShop using Qwen2.5-1.5B, 3B, and 7B-Instruct backbones against return-based process advantage baselines such as GiGPO.
sAYkoo4ufN.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that decoupling local action evaluation from downstream outcomes using action-family rubrics and state-grouped relative advantages is well motivated and practical.
sAYkoo4ufN.main_concern: Reviewers question whether gains stem from extra LLM-rubric supervision rather than the credit-assignment mechanism, note reliance on hand-crafted rubrics, and highlight single-run training without training-variance estimates.

Pe4LarfEaD.one_liner: Attributes skill-trajectory interactions across five dimensions to guard online skill library updates without model retraining.
Pe4LarfEaD.problem: Task-level outcomes in online continual agent learning do not distinguish missing activation, non-adherence, or content errors, causing direct feedback updates to corrupt reusable skills.
Pe4LarfEaD.method: AGSE attributes skill-trajectory interactions along activation, adherence, correctness, coverage, and precision without updating model weights. These structured attributions drive guarded skill repair, expansion, and scope refinement across an external skill library.
Pe4LarfEaD.key_idea: Decomposes skill-trajectory feedback into five attribution dimensions—activation, adherence, correctness, coverage, and precision—to trigger guarded edits to an external skill library.
Pe4LarfEaD.evidence: Evaluated across three heterogeneous CLI-agent frameworks on OfficeQA Pro and SkillFlow, including ablations, human validation, and continual-learning metrics.
Pe4LarfEaD.claimed_gains: Achieves exact accuracy of 72.9%, 59.4%, and 48.9% on OfficeQA Pro, completion rates of 59.64%, 49.40%, and 48.19% on SkillFlow, and continual-learning metrics of FS 67.7, FWT +0.0227, and 13.95% forgetting rate.
Pe4LarfEaD.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that separating five-dimensional skill failure attribution from guarded skill editing is a practical, well-motivated engineering approach across multiple agent harnesses.
Pe4LarfEaD.main_concern: Reviewers highlight high sensitivity to the evolution interval, small ~100-task benchmarks without multi-run variance, and lack of patch-level validation isolating whether attribution-guided edits truly fix failure causes.

ihoQ1kj6jm.one_liner: Decouples memory correction selection from write addressing via orthogonal query projection and independent gates in frozen LLMs.
ihoQ1kj6jm.problem: Compact recurrent memory modules struggle to revise stale associations without corrupting retained knowledge because key-based delta updates conflate content selection with write addressing.
ihoQ1kj6jm.method: Q-mem adds an online memory module to frozen decoder LLMs that projects a gated memory-query component orthogonal to the incoming key to select stale content for revision while using the key as the write address. Independent correction and write gates, bounded retention, and a request-local temporary state control persistence and query-conditioned access.
ihoQ1kj6jm.key_idea: Uses a gated query component orthogonal to the incoming key to select stale memory content for revision while keeping the key as the sole write address.
ihoQ1kj6jm.evidence: Evaluated across three frozen backbone models on LoCoMo against recurrent and long-term memory baselines with ablation studies.
ihoQ1kj6jm.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that decoupling what to correct from where to write via orthogonal projection and independent gates is a clean, principled design that outperforms baselines on LoCoMo.
ihoQ1kj6jm.main_concern: Reviewers question novelty relative to delta-mem and note that query-dependent correction yields only small single-seed gains over a fixed random direction on a single benchmark (LoCoMo).

pI57MPBmfK.one_liner: Constructs and selects malicious agent skills that inflate token costs via useful intermediate work while preserving task accuracy.
pI57MPBmfK.problem: Reusable agent skills can cause severe token-cost amplification that final-answer accuracy evaluations miss, while prior cost attacks can be skipped or fail to generalize across instances.
pI57MPBmfK.method: CUCKOO SKILLS pairs Autonomy-Preserving Structured Construction (APSC), which refines optional intermediate work using routing and execution feedback, with Budget-Exhaustive Risk-Sensitive Selection (BERS), which evaluates paired executions for task utility and cross-instance cost amplification.
pI57MPBmfK.key_idea: Couples routing- and execution-feedback skill construction with paired-execution risk-sensitive selection to embed useful intermediate work that inflates completion tokens without hurting task accuracy.
pI57MPBmfK.evidence: Evaluated across ARC-Challenge, LegalBench, and tau-bench on two backbone models, plus a native OpenClaw deployment on WebArena.
pI57MPBmfK.claimed_gains: Consumes 3.34–94.50x as many completion tokens as clean execution, with amplification ratios 2.57–6.90 times those of the strongest evaluated baseline.
pI57MPBmfK.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper demonstrates a practically relevant security threat with strong per-instance and native-deployment evidence showing final-answer accuracy conceals severe token abuse.
pI57MPBmfK.main_concern: Reviewers note that main tables do not separate constraint-qualified skills from unqualified fallbacks and that comparisons against prior skill/workload attacks are not budget-matched or isolated.

vfNXDvyuHM.one_liner: Adapts frozen EEG decoders once per trial via dispersion-weighted shared latent prototype shifts without labels or backpropagation.
vfNXDvyuHM.problem: Calibration-free EEG brain-computer interfaces suffer from cross-subject and non-stationary recording shifts, while per-window test-time adaptation treats overlapping windows as independent.
vfNXDvyuHM.method: TASER maps overlapping EEG windows through a frozen encoder into a latent space with source-derived temporal prototypes. After each trial prediction, it pools trial embeddings to update a shared prototype translation weighted by within-trial dispersion and window redundancy, requiring no labels, pseudo-labels, replay, or backpropagation.
vfNXDvyuHM.key_idea: Applies one label-free, gradient-free shared latent prototype translation per completed trial, weighted by within-trial embedding dispersion and window redundancy.
vfNXDvyuHM.evidence: Evaluated across nine datasets (114 participants; reviewers also note 13 datasets across MI, ERP/P300, and SSVEP) under three causal temporal protocols against ten baselines.
vfNXDvyuHM.claimed_gains: Exceeds NEO by 1.1–3.4 percentage points overall at trial completion and by 1.90–3.22 points on MI at 25/50/75% stopping settings; removing shared-shift adaptation costs 5.7–7.3 points and trial-level updating adds 1.00–1.72 points over per-window updates.
vfNXDvyuHM.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that aligning causal, label-free adaptation with BCI acquisition units and benchmarking ten methods across diverse paradigms under a unified protocol is practical and well-grounded.
vfNXDvyuHM.main_concern: Reviewers question the statistical significance and technical necessity of trial-level updates over full-trial inputs or smoothed window updates, and note modest gains outside motor imagery.

AKNWGme3EJ.one_liner: Pretrains encrypted traffic embeddings with self-supervised objectives and classifies sessions via two-stage DPI and similarity retrieval.
AKNWGme3EJ.problem: Encrypted mobile-app traffic classifiers degrade in open environments due to third-party SDK label contamination, app-update traffic drift, and unseen open-set apps.
AKNWGme3EJ.method: SimCMTC pretrains CMTE, a TCP session embedding model trained with masked sentence recovery and debiased contrastive learning. An agent runs a two-stage SimilarityDPI workflow that resolves clear sessions via domain/DPI rules and classifies remaining sessions by fusing vector-store retrieval similarity with nDPI metadata similarity.
AKNWGme3EJ.key_idea: Reformulates encrypted traffic classification as two-stage DPI filtering plus vector-store retrieval and nDPI metadata comparison over self-supervised TCP session embeddings.
AKNWGme3EJ.evidence: Evaluated across five mobile-Internet datasets spanning China, Iran, and Iraq, including closed-set, fine-tuning-free Top-1 retrieval, and end-to-end open-set evaluation on TENAPP.
AKNWGme3EJ.claimed_gains: Attains Acc/F1 of 0.910/0.898 on TENAPP under fine-tuning-free Top-1 retrieval, and reaches Acc/Macro-F1 of 0.8866/0.8833 in end-to-end open-set evaluation versus 0.8116/0.7817 for a pure DPI agent.
AKNWGme3EJ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that framing encrypted traffic classification as retrieval-and-comparison with self-supervised session embeddings is practically motivated and yields useful representations.
AKNWGme3EJ.main_concern: Reviewers point out that the fusion between vector similarity and nDPI metadata in agent decisions is underspecified and that the open-set evaluation contains no genuinely unknown apps.

d9gLASksqm.one_liner: Debiases recommendation teacher distributions via closed-form KL exposure projection and transfers them via entropic optimal transport.
d9gLASksqm.problem: Direct knowledge distillation in recommender systems propagates historical exposure and popularity bias from teachers to compact students.
d9gLASksqm.method: EOT-KD decouples teacher correction from transfer by computing a closed-form minimum-KL exposure-penalized teacher distribution using interaction frequency as an exposure proxy. It then transfers the corrected distribution to the student via entropic optimal transport with cosine-distance costs between teacher item representations.
d9gLASksqm.key_idea: Applies a closed-form KL projection to penalize expected historical exposure in teacher probabilities, then distills the corrected distribution via entropic optimal transport over teacher item-similarity costs.
d9gLASksqm.evidence: Evaluated on four recommendation benchmarks against established distillation baselines including UnKD, measuring full-catalogue ranking and long-tail metrics.
d9gLASksqm.claimed_gains: Improves Tail-NDCG@20 over the teacher by 25.9–48.9% while retaining 94.8–99.7% of the teacher's NDCG@20.
d9gLASksqm.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that separating exposure correction from similarity-aware optimal-transport distillation addresses a meaningful popularity-bias problem with reasonable four-dataset validation.
d9gLASksqm.main_concern: Reviewers view the methodological novelty as limited because the KL projection reduces to standard frequency-based logit adjustment and optimal-transport distillation has prior precedents.
